purpose: Git ignore list for the Droppy Code Xcode project: excludes macOS Finder metadata, Xcode build and per-user state artifacts, an Xcode explicit-modules compiler-cache mishap directory, the generated website app captures, Cloudflare wrangler state and Python bytecode caches.
platform_assumptions: `.DS_Store` is a macOS Finder artifact.
`DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/` and `*.xcuserstate` are Xcode-specific build and per-user UI state.

The inline comment says an Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc, so the `-Xcc/` pattern guards against a clang flag being taken as a directory name.
`build.noindex/` is the Spotlight-skipped release folder README.md names ('The disk image lands in build.noindex/, a folder Spotlight skips').
feature_notes: Exact 13 lines in order: `.DS_Store`, `build/`, `DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/`, `*.xcuserstate`, `build.noindex/`, the comment `# An Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc.`, `-Xcc/`, a blank line, the comment `# The site's app captures are generated by scripts/website_captures.py and served from R2.`, `website/assets/app/`, `.wrangler/`, `__pycache__/`.
Names the generator script by path: scripts/website_captures.py produces website/assets/app/ captures which are served from Cloudflare R2, hence ignored here.

Notably does NOT ignore `.commandcode/`, `DroppyCode.xcodeproj/`, `.build/`, `Package.resolved` or `node_modules/`; the project is generated by xcodegen from project.yml per README.md yet the .xcodeproj is not ignored.
322 bytes over 13 lines, CRLF line terminators.
unresolved_questions: Whether DroppyCode.xcodeproj is committed or merely un-ignored cannot be confirmed from this file; README.md says `xcodegen generate` produces it, which would normally suggest ignoring it, so the absence of that rule is unexplained by this bundle.

purpose: The repository's working agreement for coding agents, titled '# AGENTS.md - DroppyCode agent workflow': mandatory git-worktree isolation, the four-layer source dependency rule, what a Hydra 'head' may and may not do, a hard ban on unprompted relaunches, the glab squash-merge policy, and the release-credits requirement.
calls_into: DroppyCode/App/HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift (cited as the example of splitting a Core file that needs the provider registry into an extension one layer up)
side_effects: Prescribes `git fetch origin --prune`, `git worktree add -b <branch> ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug> origin/main`, `git worktree remove --force ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` and `git worktree prune`.
Prescribes `xcodebuild -project DroppyCode.xcodeproj -scheme DroppyCode -configuration Debug build` as the only verification step.
Prescribes `glab mr create --squash-before-merge` and `glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch`.
Prescribes `python3 scripts/release_credits.py`, whose --check mode gates scripts/publish_release.sh.
platform_assumptions: Hardcoded macOS home path `/Users/jordyspruit/Desktop/DroppyCode` as the owner's checkout that must never be edited directly.
Worktree root `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` under the Unix home directory.
`xcodebuild` plus an Xcode project and scheme, i.e. a macOS-only toolchain.
`glab` (GitLab CLI) against a GitLab-hosted project, and `python3` on PATH.
ui_elements: States the app's About cards ignore the `### Thanks` heading, so adding Thanks changes nothing on Settings > About.
feature_notes: Exact worktree path template: `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>`, branch created with `git worktree add -b <branch> ... origin/main` (or the agreed base branch).

Four-layer rule verbatim: DroppyCode/Core (models, pure support) reaches into nothing else; DroppyCode/Services (Git, Store, Providers) and DroppyCode/UI (Chrome, Common, Markdown, Theme, Sound) reach only into Core; DroppyCode/App (entry, model, runtime, windows, captures and every feature view) reaches into everything. New code goes in the lowest layer whose dependencies it has.
'There is no test target and no test scripts; the build is the check' - the upstream has no unit tests for the port to mirror.

Hydra head rule: 'A head never builds or otherwise verifies: no xcodebuild, no scripts/quick_run.sh, no check command.' It edits the files the lead briefed it on and reports, nothing more; the lead runs the one build that proves the change, in the checkout, after the heads report.

Relaunch ban is absolute: NEVER run scripts/quick_run.sh or otherwise quit/relaunch Droppy Code unless asked in that moment; building inside the worktree is fine, installing to /Applications and relaunching is not; 'Finish', 'merge', 'done' or 'test it' do not imply relaunch.

History facts stated: 4,292 commits on GitLab, mostly tiny Hydra head commits plus one merge commit per MR; the GitLab project's `merge_method` is `merge` and `squash_option` is `default_off`; every team merge MUST land as exactly one commit on main.
History rewriting (`rebase -i`, `filter-branch`, `filter-repo`, force-push to main) is forbidden; squash applies to new merges only. Never merge locally into main and never push straight to main.
Thanks bullet format is exact: `- Name (@gitlab-handle): what they did (!MR).`, placed after Refinements in every `## [x.y.z]` entry that ships outside work.
An outside merge request that lands between releases is added to `## [Unreleased]`'s Thanks right away rather than at release time.
unresolved_questions: scripts/quick_run.sh, scripts/release_credits.py and scripts/publish_release.sh are referenced but not in this bundle, so their exact flags beyond `--check` are unknown.
That quick_run.sh installs the built app to /Applications is implied by the relaunch rule's prose rather than confirmed by the script itself.

purpose: The machine-read release notes for Droppy Code: a Keep a Changelog v1.1.0 file whose `## [<version>] - <date>` sections are published verbatim as GitLab release notes and rendered as the app's Settings > About New features / Bug fixes / Refinements cards. Covers 1.0.0 (2026-09-13) through 1.6.0 (2026-09-18) plus an Unreleased section, and is the richest behavioral specification in the repository root.
calls_into: scripts/publish_release.sh (reads the section matching the version in project.yml)
scripts/build_changelog.py (builds website/changelog.json from the same sections)
side_effects: Both publish_release.sh and build_changelog.py read this file and skip `## [Unreleased]`; the next release renames that heading to its version and date.
Publishing stops until every outside contributor is named in a `### Thanks` block.
platform_assumptions: Every release headline states 'Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later. Signed and notarized.'

The Unreleased bug fix describes macOS 27 behavior: a popover's window coming on screen can make the framework's remote view throw from inside the notification that announces it, and because that happens during a SwiftUI layout pass AppKit catches the exception and stops the app; both reports came on September 18 from the release-notes cards on Settings > About.
AppKit and SwiftUI specifics recur: the window drag region computed mid layout pass, title-bar layout, traffic lights, popovers, key view loop owned by AppKit, Liquid Glass materials.
ui_elements: Settings > About cards titled 'New features', 'Bug fixes' and 'Refinements'; the Unreleased change opens their section in a card under the row instead of in a popover, folded away by tapping the card again or its close button.

Settings > General > Projects: a project mark, either an emoji or an SF Symbol; the activity list can draw that mark in front of a thread's name in place of the line that named the project, one line per thread, with what the thread is doing still at the end of the row. The list choice sits on the General page and on the welcome screen, and a new install starts on the compact one.

Usage-limit notice with two buttons: 'Cancel' stops the automatic continue and leaves the chat to you; 'New thread' stops the wait and opens a new chat of the same project holding a hand-off of the request and of what the stopped turn had already done.
Settings > Hydra > Heads: 'Auto-hide heads in the sidebar', off by default.
Settings > Hydra 'Heads at once' row of buttons: Off or 1 to 8, off by default; the uncapped choice is drawn as an infinity sign and reads as 'No cap' to VoiceOver.
Codex usage panel plan wording: account type `pro` reads 'Pro 20x' (was 'Pro'), `prolite` reads 'Pro 5x' (was 'Prolite'), and `self_serve_business_prolite` reads 'Business Premium'.
Settings > Conversation: the 'Chronological order' switch (added in 1.5.5, removed in Unreleased) and 'Show activity while working'.
The 'Worked for ...' fold line on a finished turn, with the turn's steps, its heads and its changed-files card behind it.
Banked resets row reads 'Banked resets - 2 available' on one line with the outcome of a spend below it.
Claude resume warning text: 'Claude no longer has this conversation. It starts a new one here'.
GitLab MCP failure text: 'gitlab.com didn't answer its MCP address (404), try again in a few minutes'.
Effort slider whose knob is a Liquid Glass lens; it fuses the lead's and the heads' colours for a pair.
Hydra heads' panel picker options named 'One panel' and 'A panel each'.

Keyboard: Command-W asks to archive the thread (Return archives, Escape keeps it, Delete sits beside Archive), Command-S settles it, Command-B shows and hides the sidebar, Command-1 to Command-9 switch to the first nine threads before the menu bar sees the chord, Escape stops a running turn and takes it back or dismisses whatever is in front while a field being typed in keeps its Escape.
feature_notes: Format contract in the header: 'The format follows Keep a Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versions are the release tags without the `v`', with the heading example `## [1.5.4] - 2026-09-17`.

1.6.0 scope line: folds a finished turn into its 'Worked for ...' line with the turn's steps behind the chevron, keeps a running turn's steps and the agent's thinking in the card below its bar, hands a chat stopped by its provider's usage limit a New thread that carries the work on, lets the heads leave the sidebar on their own, and puts a mark of your choosing in front of a project's name; Netlify joins the MCP catalog.
Netlify MCP connector: sign in with a Netlify account and a thread can create projects, deploy sites and manage environment variables.

GitLab MCP: a top-level group that has not allowed MCP client access is answered by GitLab 19.4 and earlier with 404 instead of 'MCP server disabled'; the app's own MCP proxy now answers a path it has no route for with 502 rather than a 404 that reads as the server's reply.
Escape on a running turn stops it and takes it back: the conversation and the provider's context rewind to before it and the message returns to the chat box; files stay as the turn left them.
Hydra head concurrency: at most eight run at a time with the rest queued, heads pace their flushes by how many are streaming, and twenty heads out at once used to freeze the app.
Head progress bars cache their staves between frames instead of walking every step of the timeline thirty times a second; three hangs of six seconds each came from that walk.
A thread opens on its last three blocks so switching to a long chat paints at once; the chat columns either side of the selected thread stay built.
Long threads run at 120 fps: rows laid out as they come into view, blocks cached, streamed chunks coalesced off the main thread.
Attachment files no thread refers to any more are swept from disk a day after they were written.
API keys live in the Keychain alone: the copy the defaults held in plain text is gone, and old copies are cleared at launch.
With 'Heads work at a working effort' on, a lead at Max on a model whose scale has no medium (Z.ai's GLM) sends its heads out at the scale's middle rung.

Themes: 26 tinted-glass themes from System to Catppuccin, Dracula, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbog, Solarized, GitHub, Matrix and Claude/Codex, plus a window transparency setting (spelling of Gruvbox in the file is 'Gruvbox').

Welcome tour: six pages of real captures at 1.2.0, eight pages of new captures over the desktop at 1.3.0 including the floating thread list and Hydra's cookbook; Help > Welcome tour and About open it again.
Banked resets: Codex at 1.3.0, Z.ai at 1.4.0 for the 5-hour and the weekly limit each with its expiry, spent after a confirm step so the limit goes back to zero.
A Debug build runs as 'Droppy Code Dev' beside the release app, with its own library and settings.

Provider arrivals: 1.0.0 Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta, Devin and Antigravity; 1.1.0 GitHub Copilot CLI with its models, efforts and monthly quotas; 1.2.0 Command Code with approvals, plan limits and remaining credits; 1.3.0 Pi with supervised, auto-accept and full-access approval levels, and Z.ai with the GLM Coding Plan.
1.3.0 records 'The license is GNU AGPL v3 with attribution'; 1.1.1 added Settings > About > Licenses shipping the app's license, third-party notices and trademark policy inside the app.
1.5.4 refinement records the four-layer source reorganisation: 'The source is arranged in four layers, Core, Services, UI and App, so a change to a model, a provider or a view has one home.'

The merge card in the timeline walks a track of dots, one per stage, that fills as the merge moves through its stages, with the head hopping along above it and a small bounce once every dot lights; finished heads and the merge pill settle with a glide transition.
1.5.6 fix: a session's ID now reaches the chat with its first message, and a session replaced before then is followed by one that starts fresh with no resume attempt and no warning.

1.6.0 Thanks names three outside contributors with exact MR numbers: Rene (@diazdesandi) !307 and !308; Bryan Galdamez (@JosueGalRe) !283, !285, !304, !306; Nikita Tsyganov (@nik1tsyganov) !293. 1.5.0 credits nik1tsyganov inline for the per-project Hydra pair rule.

!307 names concrete symbols: `search_text` confined to the project root with a `--` guard against flag smuggling, plan mode blocking edits after approve-for-turn, clearing the save timer handle before `saveNow` bails, and `WorkingTreeWatch` not tearing down the registered watch when a second caller lost the race. !308 put one OpenAI-compatible session and one Keychain behind the DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai providers.

OpenCode reports the reasoning levels of the model a session is on, so the catalog asks it for each model in turn, the way it already did for Cursor; a model catalog probe that came back empty is retried on the next ask (!306).
Claude lost-session handling: 'No conversation found with session ID' plus a CLI that exits before answering the first request is treated as a lost session and a new one begins.

Per-project Hydra pair: right-click a project in the sidebar to choose the pair each of its new chats starts on; 'The chat's last pair' removes the rule, and a pair removed from Settings takes its project rules with it.

1.5.5 head profiles: purpose-named configurations ('quick', 'deep', 'visual' or any word) with their own provider, model or effort, edited in the pair's Head profiles section in Settings; the lead hears which profiles exist and routes each task to one by name in its delegation block, and a task without a profile, or with a name the pair does not have, runs on the heads' shared model.

1.2.0 Hydra floating panels: the team's panel and any head popped out of it float over the chat, dock in any corner, stack when they share one, and can be dragged to size; a finished head wears its outcome on its glyph and every head has its own progress bar with its task and time.

1.5.1 merge scoping: each chat's merge carries only its own team's work; when a chat's work already sits on main Hydra says so and marks the heads merged; when the team's files lie outside the chat's project Hydra names the project they belong to and asks you to open the chat there.
unresolved_questions: The Unreleased section is undated and unversioned, so the next version number the port should target is not stated here; project.yml, not in this bundle, holds the version.
The prose describes behavior but not the numeric constants behind it (animation durations, panel sizes, the popover height cap named in 1.5.3); those must come from the Swift sources.
scripts/build_changelog.py and website/changelog.json are named but not in this bundle, so the JSON schema the site consumes is unknown.

hydraIsNative returns true only for .claude, .codex and .copilot; a pair that sends heads to another provider makes them Droppy-run even there (runsNatively = !elsewhere && hydraIsNative(thread.provider)).

hydraHeadsEffort: the working rung is the literal "medium" if the scale has it, else scale[(count - 1) / 2]; a lead above the working rung is tempered down to it, at or below it keeps its own; an effort not on the scale is returned unchanged; nil or empty gives nil. Comment notes Z.ai's low/high/max works out at 'high'.
The head cap is [pair?.maxHeads, settings.hydraMaxHeads].compactMap{$0}.min(); with neither, heads run uncapped.
hydraLaunch orders projects with the chat's own project first (ownRefs), then the rest.
HydraTreeCache keeps one capture per checkout for 3 seconds so a delegation block of heads shares one git add -A/write-tree; every landing calls invalidate(checkout).

Head naming and indexing: a lead whose team is empty restarts the roster (sequential = 0). A preferredIndex >= 0 is honored, stepping by HydraRoster.personas.count while that index is taken by a finished head of the team; otherwise the next free sequential index. hydraSpawnCount becomes max((pinned == nil ? index : sequential) + 1, parent.hydraSpawnCount + 1) so a pin does not shift future names.
A Droppy-run head is always created with runtimeMode = .fullAccess and fastMode = false because nobody is there to answer a permission prompt; a native head takes the lead's runtimeMode.
info.canStop = kind == .droppy || native?.taskID != nil || parent.provider == .codex.
A head in the lead's project inherits the lead's worktreePath and branch; a head sent to another project gets neither.

startDroppyHead loads the head provider's catalog and applies its default model when the head runs on a different provider with no model chosen, then makes the isolated copy, then sends the brief; a head stopped while its copy was being made never starts (guard on status == .running).

Worktree copy path: Storage.worktreesDirectory / "<project name slug>-<persona slug>-<first 8 chars of head UUID lowercased>", slugs formed by replacing spaces with '-' and lowercasing. Requires the checkout to be a git repository with commits.

Landing: diff between HydraHeadInfo.baseTree and the copy's current tree, with build output filtered from the changed-path list before any diff is made (counted as droppedBuildOutputFiles); applied three-way into the lead's checkout; only a conflict-free apply advances baseTree to the new tree.
A rebase or merge already underway in the checkout blocks landing outright: the patch is kept as a file and landing.error is set.

waitForSettledCheckout waits while the lead's phase != .idle and the wanted paths intersect hydraChatContext(for:).touchedPaths, or while the lead isHydraMerging; it polls every 250 ms up to 30 minutes, and a cancelled sleep returns immediately so the landing proceeds rather than spinning on the main actor.
Landings into one checkout are serialized through leadRuntime.hydraLanding (each new landing awaits the previous task), while patch preparation happens in parallel in each head's own copy.

Launch-failure retry: a failed turn with no tool entries whose recorded error contains "database is locked", "database locked", "sqlite_busy", "did not start a session", "the agent exited" or "stopped unexpectedly" is resent on its original brief, up to 2 retries, after Double(attempt) * 2 + Double(info.index % 4) * 0.5 seconds.
Only an error-level notice inside the just-closed turn counts as the failure cause; warnings, notes and tool output do not.
After each turn, a head on a non-API-key provider has its session stopped; API-key sessions are kept in memory so the head can be steered on with its work in mind.
Only a .completed head with its own copy lands work; stopped or failed heads keep half-done edits in their copy for a later turn.

If the user steers a head on while a landing runs, the report is dropped (guard on isRunning) and re-sent when that new turn ends; a report arriving on an already-finished head resets its status to .running first so the lead gets a fresh report.

Auto-clear finished heads (settings.hydraAutoClearFinished) waits HydraPanel.finishHold + 0.2 seconds, then unsets isInPanel and clears the lead's hydraSelectedHeadID, hydraPoppedHeadID, hydraAutoPopHeld, hydraAutoPanelDocks and the .auto(id) entry in panelStackOrder; only a .completed head also releases its copy.
releaseHydraCopy refuses while the head's runtime isRunning; it stops the session, clears worktreePath/branch/baseTree, keeps unlanded work as a patch first, then git worktree remove.

keepHydraCopyAsPatch writes nothing when the copy differs from its base only by build output or a tool's own cache: the comment records sixteen heads once producing sixteen notes for 4 GB of build output.

Watchdog: every 30 seconds over Droppy-run running heads with a live running runtime; idle >= 180 s writes 'Thinking for N min…' (rewritten only when the minute changes); idle >= 600 s with hydraEditCount == 0 and an unchanged tool count since the last look marks the head stalled and stops it. Leaving the thinking state clears the label only when it still starts with "Thinking for ".

sweepHydraCopies prunes worktrees only for projects that actually have a copy, clears worktreePath/branch/baseTree for heads whose copies vanished from disk, sweeps orphan folders, then starts the watchdog.

Orphan sweep matches "<longest matching project slug>-<persona>[-<round number>]-<8 hex chars>", skips folders any thread names and folders younger than 600 seconds, and falls back to FileManager.removeItem when git worktree remove fails.

hydraProject resolution order: empty/nil reference gives the chat's project; exact case-insensitive sidebar name; the sidebar project containing the path or equal to its standardized form (longest path wins); otherwise walk an absolute existing directory upward looking for a '.git' entry and addProject there; else nil.

hydraUnmergedFileCount unions non-running unmerged turns' touchedPaths with unmerged heads' landing files, skipping heads that finished before the last merged turn started and heads whose landing has a patchPath or error, then filters out build output and paths under no sidebar project.
hydraChatContext scans the lead's entries in reverse for the last non-Hydra user prompt and the last assistant reply, and collects deduplicated non-empty tool edit paths from the current turn only.

feature_notes: resumeHydraMerges only runs with settings.hydraAutoMerge on, over non-archived leads with hydraIsOn whose updatedAt is newer than Date.now - 3 * 24 * 3600 (3 days), idle, not already merging, with runningHydraHeads == 0, at least one completed unmerged turn and turns.last?.status == .completed; it also requires real work of its own (a completed unmerged turn with touched paths, or an unmerged head with landing files), so Hydra merely being on never sweeps someone else's changes.

The checkout never changes branch: the commit is built from git write-tree over the team's paths, committed with commitWork(tree, parent: head, message:), and the branch ref is moved with updateRef("refs/heads/<branch>", to: commit, expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head), so git refuses outright if the branch shifted.

Branch naming: "hydra/<slug>-<first 6 chars of a fresh lowercased UUID>", slug = lead title lowercased with every non letter/number mapped to '-', runs of "--" collapsed, '-' trimmed from both ends, capped at 40 characters; an untitled lead gives "team", and an empty slug falls back to "team".
On the default branch the work goes to a branch of its own that is never checked out; on any other branch the commit extends that branch and git.resetIndex(paths:) catches the index up.
Before the ref is moved, git.commitHash() is re-read and must still equal the value read at the start; otherwise the merge aborts with 'the checkout moved while it worked'.

Conflict-marker gate: a file counts as conflicted only when both "\n<<<<<<< " and "\n>>>>>>> " are found in a newline-prefixed copy of its bytes; files missing or larger than 4,000,000 bytes are skipped.

GitLab path: when Git.forge() == .gitlab and glab is on PATH, the request is created with `glab mr create --title <title> --description <body> --yes [--repo <remote web url with user and password stripped>] --source-branch <source> --target-branch <target>`. `glab auth status` is checked first; a 401/unauthorized result re-checks auth and retries the same arguments once; a failure whose output mentions 'recover' retries once with `--recover`. Everything else goes through Git.createPullRequest. Squash and remove-source-branch are left to the project's defaults.
isGitLabAuthFailure matches output containing "401" or "unauthorized", or "authentication" together with any of "failed", "expired", "invalid", "required".

hydraWork gathers three ways: unmerged turns' touchedPaths; every unmerged head's landing files plus its timeline tool edits, anchored to the head's own project checkout (a path under head.worktreePath maps to the same relative path in that checkout); and, only when sweepsCheckout is true and the first unmerged turn has a baseCheckpoint, whatever changed in the checkout since that checkpoint minus what was already dirty then.

A native head lands nothing and works in the lead's checkout, so its files come only from its timeline; a cold head's timeline is decoded off the main actor via Storage.decodeDocument rather than rehydrated as a runtime.

Path filtering order in hydraWork: drop empty and build-output paths, split into inside/outside the checkout, add the sweep's fresh paths minus sibling-owned ones, subtract sibling-owned paths, drop build output again, subtract git-ignored paths, and drop paths that neither exist on disk nor are tracked.
A head counts as unmerged when HydraHeadInfo.mergedAt is nil; a head with no mark that finished before the last merged turn began is treated as already gone out with an earlier merge.

isScratchPath treats as scratch anything under Storage.worktreesDirectory, NSTemporaryDirectory(), /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders and ~/Library, plus any dot-directory directly under home (so ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.droppy-code-dev). Both the /private and non-/private spellings of a path are tried.

An outside path is assigned to the sidebar project with the longest path that holds it, so nested checkouts resolve to the inner project; each such project gets its own merge pass with sweepsCheckout = false.

syncDefaultBranch requires a successful fetch, head to be an ancestor of origin/<target>, no dirty file among the remote's other changed paths, and HEAD still at the original commit; then reset --soft to the remote, reset the index for the team's paths, checkout the remote's version of paths present there, and remove paths gone from it. Any failure leaves the checkout untouched and returns false. presentPaths is used so one git process answers for every path.
When the lead worked in a worktree on a non-own branch, the project's own checkout is pulled fast-forward only when it is on the target branch, has no dirty paths and no operation in progress.

The commit message comes from the text engine when one is available, built from a summary of 'A'/'D'/'M' plus path lines and the patch; otherwise the lead's title (or "Hydra: the team's work" when untitled) followed by "- <Persona>: <task truncated to 100>" lines. The merge request title is TextCleanup.singleLine(message, limit: 72).
Both the whole-job patch parse and cold head timeline decoding run on Task.detached(priority: .utility) so the chat stays live.
The merge note is appended under runtime.hydraMergeNoteID so the pill's row runs from the first stage to the outcome; the id is consumed by the first note of the run and a second note gets its own.
A note only marks the thread unread, badges the Dock and notifies when the app is inactive or the lead is not the selected thread.

What the merge deliberately does not mention: files written outside the checkout, build output, ignored or missing paths and a sibling chat's files, because every line about them read as if something had gone wrong.
Any .failed project outcome aborts marking turns and heads merged; a run where every project came back .alreadyOnMain still marks them, as does a run with no groups and no stray paths.
unresolved_questions: HydraMergeStage's exact `words` strings are defined in another file, so the literal stage text on the pill is not fixed here.
Git.captureTree(paths:) semantics (whether it stages only those paths) and Git.commitWork's plumbing live in the Git layer.
HydraMergeRecord's full outcome case list beyond .merged, .failed and .stray is not established from this file.
Turn.baseCheckpoint's exact form (a tree hash versus a commit) is inferred from its use in git.changedPaths(from:to:) but not declared here.

The session is left to restart itself: the runtime launches the next turn with the pair's head definitions on its own.

hydraLead model resolution: the pair's orchestratorModel looked up in the provider's catalogue; with no lead model and a provider switch, that provider's default model; otherwise the chat's own model checked against the provider. The returned id falls back to option?.id ?? pair.orchestratorModel ?? (switchesProvider ? nil : thread.model).

hydraLead effort: the pair's orchestratorEffort wins whenever option?.efforts.contains(chosen) ?? true, so an unknown model does not block it; otherwise the remembered preference's effort only when the option's efforts contain it, else nil.
hydraLead fastMode = (option?.supportsFast ?? false) && preference.fastMode.

updateHydraPair only acts when settings actually changed (pair != before); it moves every chat with hydraIsOn leading with that pair onto the new lead model/effort/fastMode and re-remembers them, skipping chats already matching. A pair whose provider changed unpins those chats (hydraPairID = nil) instead of switching their provider, because a chat does not change provider under a conversation.

removeHydraPair unpins every thread pointing at the pair, clears settings.lastHydraPairID when it matched, and clears the pair from every Project.hydraPairID so the project's new chats fall back to the remembered pair.
setHydraPair(_:forProject:) only affects new chats in that project; open chats are untouched, and nil removes the rule.
leaveHydraPair clears the thread's hydraPairID and settings.lastHydraPairID but leaves Hydra itself as Settings has it, with heads back on the chat's own model and effort.

unarchive restores the thread and every archived helper whose parentThreadID matches, then updates the dock badge

settle refuses a settled thread or a helper, settles the thread and its helpers with a shared Date.now, clears isPinned and hasUnread, updates the dock badge, plays SettleChime when sounds && settings.settleSound, and writes the library immediately rather than on the debounce
reopen clears isSettled and settledAt, sets updatedAt = .now, clears activityOrder and activityOrderDay, un-settles the children, and saves immediately

finishSelectedThread archives (inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide)) when the finish action is .archive or when the thread is a helper; otherwise it posts a FinishRequest and waits 80 milliseconds for a sidebar row to claim it, falling back to reopenAnimated or settleAnimated
settleSelectedThread ignores helpers and uses the same 80 millisecond FinishRequest handshake

askToArchiveSelectedThread deletes outright with no question when the runtime exists and is not loading history, has no turns, no continuation, an empty draft, no followUps and is not running; otherwise it posts an ArchiveRequest and falls back to archive after 80 milliseconds

delete cascades to every child, deselects via selectNeighbor, reports an unfinished hydra head to its lead as .interrupted through finishHydraHead so the batch settles, deletes checkpoints, and removes the worktree only when removeWorktree is true or thread.hydra?.hasOwnCopy == true

deleteArchivedThreads also removes helpers of archived threads, clears the selection if it was among them, deletes all documents in one Storage.deleteDocuments call, removes checkpoints and hydra own-copy worktrees per thread, and leaves ordinary worktrees on disk exactly as a single delete does

spawnSubagent hands the prompt to an existing panel helper rather than making a second one: a running helper gets enqueueFollowUp(text:attachments: []), an idle one gets its draft set and send() called. A new helper inherits the parent's projectID, provider, model, effort, runtimeMode and fastMode, and gets parentThreadID, isInPanel = true, the given title and hasCustomTitle = true. It runs in the project folder itself so a merge lands on the main checkout, never in a thread's worktree.

closeSubagent interrupts a running helper and defers stopSession until the turn finishes by inserting the id into sessionsToRelease, then sets isInPanel = false so the helper moves to the sidebar under its parent

createWorktree refuses when the thread already has a worktree, or when the folder is not a git repository or has no commits (showing the "Worktree unavailable" alert). The path is Storage.worktreesDirectory / "<project name with spaces replaced by '-' and lowercased>-<first 8 chars of the lowercased thread uuid>", the branch is "droppy-code/<the same 8 chars>", based on the current git branch. On success it runs every project script with runOnWorktreeCreate == true in the new directory and shows the terminal.

isOnScreen: true for the selected thread itself; for a child of the selection, true when it is in a panel and not archived; otherwise true only when the child and its parent are not archived, the parent is not in a panel, does not fold helpers and is not settled, matching what SidebarView shows inline

threadNeedsAttention marks the thread read instead of notifying when NSApp.isActive and the thread is on screen; otherwise it notifies with body "Waiting for your decision." and calls NSApp.requestUserAttention(.informationalRequest)

turnFinished writes lastStatus and updatedAt, and sets hasUnread = !isVisible except for hydra heads which never mark themselves; releases a deferred session from sessionsToRelease; returns early when autoContinue.turnFinished took the turn (a spent usage limit waits for the reset with no chime and no error banner); a hydra head reports to its lead via hydraHeadTurnFinished only when continues == false, and returns either way

Chime rule: chimed = settings.chimeWhenFinished && status != .interrupted, so a stop the user asked for is silent. When the chime sounded, the notification is posted with sound: nil so the banner does not double it; otherwise sound: .default
The notification is only posted when the thread is not visible and settings.notifyWhenFinished is true
markRead([UUID]) coalesces many threads into a single library write, so the cells and the sidebar see one change rather than one per thread
notify() is skipped entirely when WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, and skipped when NSApp.isActive and the thread is on screen
requestNotificationPermission asks once (didRequestNotifications) for [.alert, .sound, .badge]
updateDockBadge counts threads where hasUnread && !isArchived && !isInPanel

textEngine: .off returns nil; .claude returns claude(); .codex returns codex(); .automatic returns codex() ?? claude() when the preferred provider is .codex, otherwise claude() ?? codex(). Each engine needs providers.status(kind).auth != .signedOut and a resolved executable; codex additionally needs providers.defaultModel(for: .codex)?.id.

storeAPIKeyFallback trims the value and removes the defaults entry when it is empty, so a key the Keychain holds never sits in defaults too
updateHydraPair clamps the edited pair's maxHeads through HydraPair.clampedCap and skips the write when the pair is unchanged

addToModelList refuses duplicates and anything past modelListLimit (15)
moveModel computes dest = to + (placeAfter ? 1 : 0), then decrements dest when from < dest, returns false when from == dest, and otherwise removes and reinserts the pin

hydraPairs decode leniently through Lenient<HydraPair> with compactMap(\.value), so one unreadable pair does not lose the rest

hydraTempersHeadEffort (default true) makes heads think at a working effort rather than the lead's own: a lead above medium sends out medium heads on the same model, and a scale with no medium works out at its middle rung, unless the pair names a head effort

hydraIsolateHeads (default true) gives each Droppy-run head its own copy of the checkout so no head sees another's half-done work; its changes land in the chat's checkout when it reports. Off, the heads work in the checkout itself.
hydraAlwaysHeads sends every user message to a head, sent or queued, idle lead or not, so the lead only hears the heads' reports; when every head is busy a message goes the ordinary way
hydraQueueHeads sends a follow-up queued during a running turn straight to a head instead of waiting for the turn
hydraAutoMerge, when on, sends the team's work out as a merge request once the lead has finished and every head is back, and brings the checkout up to date
hydraReviewHeads makes the lead audit every head's landed work before finishing, reading the files the reports name and correcting what is wrong
hydraAutoPopsHeads gives each head after the first a panel of its own on the left and right while there is room beside the chat (see PanelScene.autoPopped)
showsUsagePanel is set by the General setting, the usage popover's pop-out button and the panel's own close button, so it persists across threads and relaunches
hydraDefaultEnabled is stored under ChatThread.hydraDefaultKey because ChatThread seeds new threads from it before any AppSettings object exists; it is true until the user first switches a chat off
The theme read falls back from the appTheme key to the legacy appearance key before defaulting to .system, and ThemeManager.current is set from the initial value inside init

Verification is threefold on the copied-out app: Developer ID signature for team NARHG44L48 with identifier equal to Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier (fallback literal "iordv.droppycode"), CFBundleShortVersionString equal to the accepted update version, and spctl Gatekeeper acceptance

Installer script waits for the PID with kill -0 in 0.25 s steps, giving up after i > 240 (about 60 seconds) with the message "The app did not quit"; it also prints "Could not move the installed app aside" and "Could not move the update into place"
Backup path used by the script: "$(dirname "$DEST")/.$(basename "$DEST").previous"; it is restored if the move-in fails and removed on success
The staged app is copied to a path whose last component equals Bundle.main.bundleURL.lastPathComponent, so the installed bundle keeps its filename
The 25 s handoff timeout clears the relaunch marker and calls fail() if the app is somehow still in .handoff (a refused quit)
Downloader is a URLSessionDownloadDelegate so a large image streams to disk; didFinishDownloadingTo moves the temp file immediately and rejects non-2xx responses

purpose: The SwiftUI @main entry point: runs the fixed-order launch prologue (notification guard, SIGPIPE ignore, capture prep, legacy migration, hang watchdog, switch latency) and declares a menus-only Settings scene, because the real windows are AppKit windows owned by WindowManager.

side_effects: Installs a framework notification guard before anything posts a notification (DCInstallNotificationGuard)
Sets the SIGPIPE disposition to SIG_IGN process-wide so writes to an exited provider process report EPIPE instead of killing the app
WebsiteCaptures.prepare() runs before any settings or library read
LegacyMigration.run() migrates defaults and the support folder from the former app name
HangWatchdog.start() writes main-thread stacks to ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code when the main thread freezes
SwitchLatency.start()
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI App lifecycle bridged to AppKit with @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor
Settings scene, a macOS-only SwiftUI scene type, used purely as a menu carrier with EmptyView content
POSIX signal(3) with SIGPIPE / SIG_IGN
Log destination ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code (macOS user Logs directory)
Comment cites popover window ordering on macOS 27 as the reason for the notification guard
Real windows are AppKit NSWindows owned by WindowManager, not SwiftUI WindowGroups
ui_elements: Settings { EmptyView() } scene carrying .commands { AppCommands(model: WindowManager.shared.model) } — no SwiftUI-declared app windows at all
feature_notes: Launch order is explicitly load-bearing and commented: DCInstallNotificationGuard() first (before anything posts a notification), then SIGPIPE ignore, then WebsiteCaptures.prepare() and LegacyMigration.run() before anything reads settings or the library, then HangWatchdog.start() and SwitchLatency.start()
A framework observer raising while a notification is posted costs a log line instead of the app, per the guard's comment
The menu bar contents come entirely from AppCommands built over WindowManager.shared.model
unresolved_questions: AppDelegate, DCInstallNotificationGuard, WebsiteCaptures, HangWatchdog, SwitchLatency, WindowManager and AppCommands are all defined outside this bundle, so what each prologue step actually does is not verifiable from this file

purpose: The app-layer half of HydraCookbook, kept apart from the recipes themselves because it needs the provider registry and settings: it turns a declarative HydraPairRecipe into a concrete HydraPair on this particular Mac, choosing the newest catalogue model whose name or id contains one of the recipe's name fragments, and naming the provider a recipe still needs.

HydraPair(provider:) with orchestratorModel, orchestratorEffort, workerProvider, workerModel, workerEffort, maxHeads
effort(_:for:) - a HydraCookbook helper declared in the companion file
state_owned: None: every member is a pure static function over the registry and settings handed in
side_effects: None: no file writes, process launches, network calls, notifications, timers or keychain access
platform_assumptions: @MainActor isolation for reading the provider registry and settings
Foundation's localizedCaseInsensitiveContains for fragment matching
Swift regex literal #/[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?/# with firstMatch(of:) for version parsing
persisted_fields: Reads settings.isEnabled(provider) only; writes nothing. The HydraPair it returns is persisted by its caller.
ui_elements: missingProvider names the provider a recipe row should offer to set up: the first listed provider of the first side (lead before heads) with nothing ready
A recipe where either side has no ready provider listing its model resolves to nil, so its row cannot be used
feature_notes: isReady = settings.isEnabled(provider) && registry.status(provider).isInstalled. Note this uses status().isInstalled, unlike AppModel.hydraPickerPairs which uses countsAsInstalled, so an unprobed provider is not ready here.
provider(for:) takes the first of a side's providers that is ready and, when the side names models, actually lists one of them (side.models.isEmpty short-circuits that check).
missingProvider ignores whether the model is listed: it reports the first side whose providers are all unready, returning that side's first provider.

resolve builds HydraPair(provider: leadProvider), sets orchestratorModel to the resolved lead model's id and orchestratorEffort from recipe.lead.effort against that model (or the registry default model when the named one was not found), sets workerProvider only when the heads' provider differs from the lead's, sets workerModel/workerEffort the same way for the heads side, and copies recipe.maxHeads.

model(named:) treats each entry of names as a family fragment matched case-insensitively against a ModelOption's name or id; among the matches the highest first version number in the name wins, with ties broken by the later position in registry.models(for:) (options.firstIndex(where:)! > options.firstIndex(where:)!), so a new release moves a recipe up on its own.
The fragments are tried in order and the first fragment with any match returns immediately, so later fragments are pure fallbacks.
version(of:) reads the first [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)? match in a catalogue name, so 'Gemini 3.8 Flash' gives 3.8; a name with no digits scores -1 in the comparison and loses to any numbered name.
unresolved_questions: The effort(_:for:) helper used for both sides is declared in the companion HydraCookbook file, so how a recipe's effort word maps onto a model's scale is not visible here.
HydraPairRecipe.Side's exact field types (especially the type of `effort`) and the full built-in recipe list are defined elsewhere.
Whether options.firstIndex(where:)! could ever trap is not determinable here; it indexes back into the same `options` array the matches came from, which appears safe but is not proven in this file.

purpose: Defines the @MainActor @Observable class AutoContinue, the runtime service that resumes a chat automatically once its provider's usage-limit window resets: it records limit hits during a turn (noteLimit), decides at turn end whether to start a wait (turnFinished), sleeps until the reset time plus a 60 second margin, posts notices and notifications, then enqueues and immediately sends a fixed continue prompt. It also implements user-driven cancel and hand-off into a new chat.

Creates a new thread in the project (AppModel.newThread(in:)) and writes its composer draft text during handOff
Enqueues and immediately sends a follow-up prompt (enqueueFollowUp then sendFollowUpNow), which starts a new provider turn

settings.notifyWhenFinished: Bool - gate for the system notification in notify(_:_:)

ui_elements: Info notice text: "Usage limit reached. Continuing automatically at \(when)." posted with notice.limit = LimitNotice(threadID:) set, which is what makes the transcript row show the countdown
Warning notice text when no reset time is known: "Usage limit reached, and the provider did not say when it resets. Send a message to continue."
Notification body when a time is known: "Usage limit reached. Continuing at \(when)."
Notification body when no time is known: "Usage limit reached. Send a message to continue."
Notification title is the thread's title (thread.title)
The follow-up message that appears in the chat: "The usage limit has reset. Continue exactly where you left off and finish the task."
The time string comes from AutoContinue.format(_:), which forwards to UsageLimitSignal.format(_:)
outcomes drives the wording the notice row shows after the wait ends (.cancelled / .handedOff(newThreadID) / .resumed), per the doc comment on LimitOutcome
feature_notes: continueMessage is identical for every provider: "The usage limit has reset. Continue exactly where you left off and finish the task."
margin is exactly 60 seconds (TimeInterval) past the provider's stated reset time
The resume moment is max(resetsAt.addingTimeInterval(60), Date.now.addingTimeInterval(5)): a reset already in the past still waits at least 5 seconds
noteLimit keeps the better note: if an entry already exists and is non-nil while the new resetsAt is nil, the new note is ignored; otherwise it overwrites
turnFinished consumes the note with removeValue(forKey:) and returns false when there was no note, so a failure without a limit hit is reported normally

A wait only starts when all hold: a note exists, settings.autoContinueAfterLimit is on, status == .failed, continues == false, the thread exists, and !thread.isHydraHead (Hydra heads are left to their leads)
turnFinished returning true tells the app not to chime or notify about the failure
Any previous wait for the thread is cancelled and outcomes[threadID] is reset to nil before the new wait starts

The turn being resumed is pinned by turnID = app.existingRuntime(for: threadID)?.turns.last?.id; after the sleep the resume is skipped if runtime.turns.last?.id != turnID, meaning the user already picked the chat up themselves
Resume is also skipped if the runtime no longer exists, runtime.isRunning is true, or settings.autoContinueAfterLimit was turned off during the wait

Generation tokens: waitTokens[threadID] == token is checked after the readResetTime await and again after the sleep; a superseded or cancelled wait returns without touching resumesAt, waits or waitTokens
When the turn itself gave no reset time, readResetTime queries the provider's live plan limits and picks the window with the highest percent among windows whose resetsAt is non-nil and in the future
That window is only accepted when spent.percent >= 95; otherwise readResetTime returns nil and the warning notice path runs
readResetTime returns nil unless PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits(provider); for API-key providers an empty stored key returns nil, and for CLI providers a missing executable returns nil
cancel(_:) cancels the task, clears waits, waitTokens and resumesAt, and records LimitOutcome.cancelled

handOff(_:) builds LimitHandoff.text(for: runtime, title: thread.title), calls cancel(threadID), creates a new thread in the same project, records .handedOff(made.id) and sets app.runtime(for: made.id).draft.text to the hand-off text; the user chooses the model and sends it themselves
handOff records .handedOff after cancel has already written .cancelled, so the hand-off outcome wins; if project(_:) or newThread(in:) returns nil the outcome stays .cancelled
The resume sends by finding the last queued follow-up whose text equals continueMessage and calling runtime.sendFollowUpNow(prompt.id)
notify suppresses the notification when NSApp.isActive and app.selectedThreadID == threadID (the onScreen check)

The exact string produced by UsageLimitSignal.format(_:) (date style, locale handling) is defined in another file
PlanLimits.Window.percent's scale is assumed to be 0 to 100 because of the >= 95 comparison, but the type is not declared here
Nothing in this file cancels all waits on teardown or app quit, so whether waits survive window or app-level teardown cannot be determined here

purpose: A stateless namespace enum that renders the plain-text hand-off prompt placed into a new chat's composer when a chat stopped on its provider's usage limit: it restates the request being answered, up to 40 bullet lines of what the stopped turn had already said and run, and up to 20 changed file paths, then asks the new model to take the work over.

private static func flatten(_ text: String) -> String
calls_into: Entry content cases matched: .user(message) with message.text, .assistant(message) with message.text, .tool(call) with call.title and call.edits
state_owned: None: the enum has no cases and no stored properties; text(for:title:) uses only the locals turnID, turn, request, requestText, lines, seen, suffix, paths and blocks
side_effects: None: pure string building, no file writes, process launches, network calls, notifications, timers or keychain access

import Foundation only; no AppKit or SwiftUI, so the formatting logic itself is portable apart from the runtime model it reads
Swift pattern matching over the entry content enum plus Collection prefix/joined/components(separatedBy:) APIs
persisted_fields: None: nothing is read from or written to UserDefaults or disk; the produced text is placed into a composer draft by the caller, AutoContinue.handOff
ui_elements: Opening block (exact): Continue the work from the chat "<title>". It stopped when its provider's usage limit was reached, and it will not continue there. - the title is wrapped in straight double quotes
Request block header (exact): "The request it was answering:" followed by a blank line and the request text
Fallback request text (exact): "(the request was not recorded)"
Work block header (exact): "What it had already done in that turn:" followed by a blank line and the bullet lines
Files block header (exact): "Files it had changed:" followed by a blank line and "- " prefixed paths
Closing block (exact): "Take it over from here and finish it, asking me about anything unclear."
Assistant bullet prefix (exact, trailing space included): "- It said: "
Tool bullet prefix (exact, trailing space included): "- It ran: "
Changed-files suffix on a tool bullet (exact): " (changed <suffix>)"
Overflow phrase inside a tool bullet (exact): " and <n> more" where n = seen.count - 5

Blocks are joined with "

"; bullet lines and path lines are joined with "
"; edit paths inside a tool bullet are joined with ", "
feature_notes: The turn scanned is the last one: turn = entries whose turnID == runtime.turns.last?.id; when there is no last turn it falls back to the whole entries list
The request is found by scanning runtime.entries.reversed() (the whole transcript, not just the last turn) for the most recent .user entry and flattening its text
At most 40 bullet lines are produced: the loop breaks once lines.count reaches 40 (guard lines.count < 40 else { break })
Assistant text longer than 400 characters is truncated to String(flat.prefix(400)) and suffixed with the single character U+2026 horizontal ellipsis
Assistant entries whose flattened text is empty are skipped entirely (continue), and do not consume one of the 40 line slots
A tool bullet lists at most 5 distinct changed paths (seen.prefix(5) joined by ", "); beyond that it appends " and N more" where N = seen.count - 5
Distinct paths per tool call are collected in first-seen order with a linear !seen.contains(edit.path) check
The global Files-it-had-changed list collects distinct edit paths across the turn's tool calls and stops at exactly 20, checked both inside the inner edit loop and again after each entry
The work block and the files block are omitted entirely when their lists are empty; the opening, request and closing blocks are always present
Entry contents other than .user, .assistant and .tool are ignored (default: break in the switch)
flatten collapses all whitespace and newlines: components(separatedBy: .whitespacesAndNewlines), drop empty pieces, join with a single space, so multi-line messages become one line
unresolved_questions: The concrete shape of the entry content enum (whether .user and .assistant carry the same message type) and of the tool call's title and edits is defined in other files
Whether call.title is already user-facing prose (it is embedded verbatim after "- It ran: ") or a raw tool identifier cannot be determined from this file
The request scan ignores turn boundaries, so it picks the newest user message anywhere in the transcript; whether that can ever differ from the last turn's request is not determinable here

takeBackRunningTurn: Escape on a running turn stops it and rewinds with revert(to:restoreFiles: false), returning the message text and attachments to the composer; it polls for idle up to 200 times at 50 ms and gives up if the draft is no longer empty, heads are working, the message isFromHydra, or the turn left the thread; files stay as the turn left them

Head time budget: HydraBudget.maxSeconds plus 90 extra seconds when the head's provider isAPIKeyBased; a final report turn uses HydraBudget.reportSeconds; on expiry the head is interrupted and its next turn is HydraBudget.finalNote

apiTranscript(): keeps the last 40 messages via suffix(40) within a 60_000 character budget; a message that does not fit is truncated to an ellipsis plus its last budget characters when budget > 200, otherwise everything up to and including it is dropped; consecutive assistant fragments are joined with "\n\n" and tool calls are excluded

Diff caches: turnDiffs RecentCache(limit: 64) keyed by finished turn id, revisionDiffs RecentCache(limit: 4) keyed by the selection uuidString or the literal "all"; revertPreviews are valid for 10 seconds and only within the current diffRevision

updateAvailable is recomputed from the running version, so an installed update stops reading as available while the notes stay
startBackgroundChecks() is a no-op if already started, if WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, or if AppInfo.isDevelopment; it waits 8 s after launch then checks every 6 hours (21600 s)
Becoming active triggers a catch-up check only when the last check is older than 6 hours, or when there has never been one
check() returns early with updateAvailable when a check is already running, and returns false outright in development builds

newestRelease(in:) skips releases where upcomingRelease is true, where the tag does not parse, where releasedAt is in the future, where no asset link is a disk image, or where the URL will not parse; among the rest it keeps the highest version (ties keep the first, since `if let current = best, current.0 >= version { continue }`)
Link.isDiskImage is true when the lowercased direct_asset_url-or-url path ends in ".dmg" or the lowercased asset name ends in ".dmg"
pageURL is releasesURL.appending(path: release.tagName), i.e. https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases/<tag>

The launch flag `--preview-update 9.9.9` overrides only the reported version of the real newest release, so the update story can be demonstrated; installing it then fails verification unless the real release carries that version
size is filled in by a HEAD request only when the release JSON did not supply one; nothing depends on it
notifyOnce marks the version as notified BEFORE the async add, so a denied or failed add still suppresses future banners for that version

feature_notes: Files line regex (the thing that makes a body a merge note): ^(\d+) files? \(\+(\d+) −(\d+)\) landed on `([^`]+)` from `([^`]+)`\.$ - note the U+2212 minus sign and the backticked target and branch; without a match parse returns nil and the caller keeps the generic popover

Head line regex: ^- (.+?) \((\d+)\): (.*?) — (?:no files|(\d+) files?: (.*))$ - name, persona index, task, em dash separator, then either the literal 'no files' or a count and a comma-space separated file list
Parsing: a line exactly equal to 'Heads' starts the heads section; a blank line ends it; a non '- ' line ends it too; only the first files line is taken (match == nil guard)
A line ending in 'is up to date.' is dropped as not a note; every other leftover line becomes a note with all backticks stripped
Open button title by forge: 'Open merge request' for .gitlab, 'Open pull request' for .github and .gitea
Copy link is guarded against re-entry while didCopyLink is true; the Copied state lasts 1.4 s
Each head face carries its own popover so the card hangs from the face under the cursor; hover sets hoveredHead and clears it only if it is still that head

Timings: rise 0.45 s (ease-out cubic 1 - pow(1 - t, 3)), sweep 2.6 s, sweepRest 3.4 s, clock 1/24 s; sweepSlots 3
Stave height shares: lookup 0.45, command 0.65, edit 0.85, reply 1

Stave colours: edit and reply full tint, command tint.opacity(0.7), lookup tint.opacity(0.4); a failed head's last stave is Chrome.danger, a stopped head's last stave Chrome.secondaryText; the hovered stave is overpainted .white.opacity(0.4)
Empty slots: height bottom * 0.45, filled Chrome.overlay(0.06), drawn for indices staves.count..<capacity

Sweep band: width max(24, filledWidth / 3) where filledWidth = count * pitch - gap; clipped to the filled path; linear gradient white 0 -> white 0.55 -> white 0; x = -band + phase * (filledWidth + band)

Hover card: width 260, HStack spacing 8, MCPGlyph size 14 or SF symbol .system(size: 12, weight: .semibold) secondary in a 14-wide frame, step text .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold) primary lineLimit 1 truncation .tail; padding horizontal 12 / vertical 10; ProgressCardSurface at Chrome.cardCornerRadius; padding(.bottom, 8) in a zero-height bottom-aligned frame; x clamped to [0, width - 260]; allowsHitTesting(false); transition .opacity; animation .smooth(duration: 0.15) on hoveredIndex

feature_notes: Stave kinds from tool calls: .edit kind -> edit; .command kind -> command unless call.edits is non-empty, then edit; any other kind -> lookup unless call.edits is non-empty, then edit; an assistant message becomes a reply stave
Reply stave label: TextCleanup.singleLine of only the first 600 characters, limit 60, rendered as 'Replied: <words>' or plain 'Replied' when empty; symbol 'bubble.left'
Tool stave label is ToolPresentation.label(for: call); its mark is the MCP server's glyph when ToolPresentation.mcpParts(call) resolves, otherwise ToolPresentation.symbol(for: call.kind)

feature_notes: Head section headers are markdown '## Name: task ...'; a '## ' line only starts a head when the text before its first colon resolves through HydraRoster.index(named:), so a head's own '## ' headings stay inside its body

Trailing parenthesised groups on a header are peeled right-to-left and treated as metadata only when: lowercased == "failed", lowercased hasPrefix "stopped", the group contains a decimal digit, or the group is in the effort set {"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "minimal", "fast", "default"}; otherwise peeling stops and the rest is the task
Effort groups are joined with " \u00b7 " and, inside a group, ", " is replaced with " \u00b7 "; efforts are inserted at index 0 so original left-to-right order is preserved
Landing line prefixes recognized: "Landed in your checkout:", "Did not land", "Changed nothing.", "Nothing landed"
"Nothing landed ... in its copy at <path>" yields .unfinished(copyPath:) with a trailing period stripped; the marker searched for is the literal "in its copy at "
"Did not land (<error>): <files>" parses the parenthesised error; an empty error becomes nil
File item regex literal: ^(\\S+) \\(\\+(\\d+) [\u2212\\-](\\d+)\\)( with conflicts)?$ ; the lead writes U+2212 but ASCII hyphen also matches
Before splitting on ", ", these tails are stripped by regex, longest first: "; \\d+ build-output files? (was|were) left out$" then ", and \\d+ more$"; a trailing "." is stripped first

The lead's closing instructions are dropped from the LAST head's body only: the final paragraph (after the last blank-line break) is removed if it starts with any of "The changes listed above", "The heads worked in your checkout", "A file listed with conflicts", "Do not check any of this", "Do not wait for", "A head that failed", "A head the user stopped", "The user queued", "The user sent"

One head: header carries the head, the card is not collapsible, its report is expanded and its blocks parsed synchronously in init; several heads: cards are collapsible, start collapsed, and bodies warm in the background
Totals line format: "<N> head(s)" and, when any files, " \u00b7 <F> file(s) \u00b7 +<A> \u2212<D>"; files line for a single head: "<F> file(s) \u00b7 +<A> \u2212<D>"
The intro sentence containing the literal substring "still at work" is extracted from the character after the previous "." to the end of the intro and shown under the title
cleanedTitle removes repeated "Name: " or "Name " prefixes while at least two remain, leaving exactly one; withoutNamePrefix removes a single leading "Name: "
hasReport is false when the body is empty or exactly "No report."
Persona lookup order for a head: match in the passed personas by name, else HydraRoster.persona(named:), else HydraRoster.persona(at: 0)
Outcome to HydraHeadInfo.Status mapping for the glyph: done -> .completed, failed -> .failed, stopped -> .stopped

Scope.isPartial is true when hasUnloadedHistory, or (tokens == nil ? turns > 0 : turnsWithUsage < turns)
recordedTokens is nil only when both lead and heads recorded nothing; otherwise the present side(s) are summed
spansProviders is true when the set of providers across lead.groups + heads.groups has more than one element

sitsBesideComposer: pane.width - 2*20 - panelWidth - 12 >= 360; otherwise the panel docks above the composer and composerReserve is 0
fitsBothSides: pane.width - 2*20 - 2*(panelWidth + 12) >= 360; below that, panels dock on one side only (comment points at PanelScene.lockedSide)

dockedOrigin when beside the composer centres the composer in the row left after both reserves: row = pane.width - reserve.leading - reserve.trailing, composerWidth = min(820, row - 40), composerLeft = reserve.leading + (row - composerWidth)/2; leading panel at composerLeft - 12 - panelWidth, trailing at composerLeft + composerWidth + 12
dockedOrigin when not beside the composer: x = 20 for leading, pane.width - 20 - panelWidth for trailing
dockedOrigin y: Chrome.contentTopInset for a top corner, else pane.height - (sitsBesideComposer ? 14 : composerAreaHeight + 12) - panelHeight

dockCorner hysteresis: the centre must be more than 56 points past the pane middle on an axis to change side or top/bottom, otherwise the current corner is kept; the middle's y is (docks.topLeading.y + docks.bottomLeading.y + panelHeight)/2

PanelDocks.stacked spreads a side's slots evenly between the top and bottom docked y; step = (bottomLeading.y - topLeading.y)/(slots-1); a top-corner panel with below = b sits at slot b, a bottom-corner one at slot slots-1-b; x comes from the corner itself
PanelDocks.corner(forSlot:of:side:): slots with index <= (slots-1)/2 go to the side's top corner with below = index, the rest to the bottom corner with below = slots-1-index
slotIndex rounds (origin.y - topLeading.y)/step and clamps to 0...slots-1; returns 0 when step <= 0
Drag velocity is an exponential blend: velocity = 0.4*previous + 0.6*instant, and readings closer together than 0.004 s are ignored as same-frame events

Flick: release() returns position + velocity * 0.12 (flickCarry), unless at least 0.08 s (restBeforeDrop) has passed since the last move, in which case the panel drops exactly where it is; nil when never moved

PanelPlacement animates with Chrome.panelSlide only when settling: drag.position == nil, not resizing and not in a window live resize; otherwise animation is nil so the panel tracks the pointer and the live resize exactly; both origin and size are animated
SubagentPanel .animation(nil, value: liveResize.isActive) keeps the frame following the pane every live-resize frame

Resize grips sit on the two edges away from the dock corner; the free corner's cursor is the opposite of the dock corner (topLeading -> bottomRight, topTrailing -> bottomLeft, bottomLeading -> topRight, bottomTrailing -> topLeft)
Double-clicking a grip calls onReset (back to the automatic size); the double click fires in mouseDown on clickCount == 2
PanelDragHandleView.acceptsFirstMouse returns true so the first click takes hold even when the window is not key, and mouseDownCanMoveWindow is false so a press moves the panel rather than the window

The working box shows the sending pulse for about 0.9 s after isRunning turns true, then settles into "<name> working"; both state changes animate with Chrome.panelSlide unless a live resize is active

feature_notes: Lazy window: first paint shows TimelineWindow.firstPaint = 3 blocks, grows to TimelineWindow.initial = 24 after a 250ms sleep in .task(id: runtime.threadID), then TimelineWindow.page = 24 more blocks per load; loadEarlier sets historyLoadPending and forces anchorsBottomOnGrowth = true so incoming history lands above the viewport without moving the reader

Follow-the-end logic: pinned when distanceFromBottom < 48; anchorsBottomOnGrowth chooses .bottom vs .top for .sizeChanges; a reader move is detected when abs((new.offset - old.offset) - anchorMove) > 1

Scrolling past the end (distanceFromBottom < -1) while at rest and only when contentHeight or containerHeight changed in the same frame snaps to the bottom, deferred through DispatchQueue.main.async with a disablesAnimations transaction

On runtime.isRunning becoming true: a send or a turn for a reader already at the end snaps/animates to the bottom (unanimated when already there, withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.25)) otherwise); an unattended turn (runtime.autoStartedTurnToken differs from seenAutoStartedTurnToken) for a reader who scrolled up does not pull them down

repairLayout escalation for a blank viewport: blankRepairs 0 -> refreshViewport(), 1 -> stackGeneration += 1 plus armViewportRefresh(), 2 -> pin and snap to the bottom plus armViewportRefresh(), 3 and beyond -> give up; any row reporting itself visible cancels the blank watch and resets blankRepairs to 0

refreshViewport 'nudge': beginNudge tries offsets of -1 then +1 points (accepted when abs(target.y - origin.y) > 0.25), restoreNudge puts the clip view back and re-snaps to the bottom if pinned; nudgePhase runs 0 -> 1 (moved) -> 2 (scroll view reported) -> 3 (moving back) -> 0
armViewportRefresh throttling: a burst resets after 2 seconds of quiet and allows at most 8 refreshes per burst
Drift accounting: noteDrift accumulates shrink + drift and fires when it passes jumpTolerance = max(48, viewportHeight / 4); a reader's own scroll resets drift to 0

Scroll freeze: isReaderScrolling turns off hit-testing on the rows via the ScrollFreeze leaf modifier (comment says hover re-hit-testing was about a fifth of the main thread's scroll-time work); it lifts 150ms after the last moving frame, polled every 80ms

Lost scroll phases: a .interacting phase with no reader movement for 2.0s, or a coast with none for 0.4s, or any phase running past 3.0s, is treated as over, reports scrolling false and bumps checkRequest

Minimap jump: jump(to:in:animated:) expands visibleCount to reach a target above the window, sets historyLoadPending, then scrolls to the block id with anchor .top inside withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.35)) (or a disablesAnimations transaction when not animated), deferring through DispatchQueue.main.async when the window had to expand
The rail's active tick: resolveActive() takes the middle element of the on-screen run (onScreen[onScreen.count / 2]) and lights the last user block at or above it

Block identity scheme: turn blocks are "turn-<turnID.uuidString>-<first row entry id>", work groups "work-<first entry id>", heads groups "heads-<first entry id>", working "working-<turnID uuidString or empty>", heads-working "hydra-heads-working" or "hydra-heads-working-tail" when trailing

Hydra merge pill: the timeline appends .merging(id:) using runtime.hydraMergeNoteID or the fallback literal "hydra-merging" while runtime.isHydraMerging, and suppresses it once the last entry is a merge outcome; a merge outcome is a user message with isFromHydra true, no hydraHeads, and a first line starting with the literal "Hydra "

Head pills: finished heads are sorted by finishedAt, split at runtime.turnStartedAt into earlier (inserted above the running turn block, only when that turn has no head rows) and later (appended, trailing: isRunning)

Block cache fast path: the cache key is entry ObjectIdentifiers plus turnEnd count, isRunning, hydraMergeID, pills and showReasoning; an append-only key change rebuilds only the last run (buildTail) and keeps earlier blocks, returning nil when a new end marker would fold an already stable turn block; in DEBUG every 20th tail build is compared against a full build and falls back on a mismatch
TimelineBlockCache keeps at most 24 per-thread caches in LRU order
Turn folding: a turn block renders TurnRunningBlock until a TurnSummary exists, then TurnFinishedBlock, both with .transition(.identity) so no fade composites a very tall layer

Transitions: .turn blocks with a summary and work groups of more than softAppearLimit = 8 entries get .identity; everything else gets rowTransition = asymmetric(insertion: SoftAppearModifier(isVisible: false) -> (isVisible: true) animated with .softAppear, removal: .identity)
Reasoning entries never render as rows of their own; they appear only behind the working indicator's chevron, and only when model.settings.showReasoning is on
A work run that has a reply after it starts collapsed (startsCollapsed computed from replyIndices)
Tool entries of kind .agent are pulled out of the work run into a trailing .heads group
Composer growth (scrollState.areaGrowthRequest) only pulls a reader who is pinned or within 48 points of the end, and is skipped while liveResize.isActive
Question badges: when runtime.questions.count drops from non-zero to 0 the timeline arms a viewport refresh; a new question badge pulls any reader to the end regardless of pinning

FrontMonitor.concerns(_:) distinguishes the app becoming active (app-wide, affects every timeline) from a specific window being uncovered, so a popover or tooltip opening over the chat no longer triggers a self-repair
ScrollMetrics reports distanceFromBottom = 0 when contentSize.height + insets <= containerSize.height + 1, and clamps travel to the actual scrollable excess

purpose: Implements the chat timeline minimap: the slim vertical rail on the left edge of the chat column that draws one small tick per message the user sent, lights the tick for the block currently on screen, shows a Liquid Glass preview card on hover, and lets the reader tap or drag-scrub to jump to a message. Contains the outline model (TimelineMinimapEntry), the outline builder with its title/snippet/weight heuristics (enum TimelineMinimap), three layered views for render-cost isolation (TimelineMinimapColumn, MinimapSelection, TimelineMinimapRail), the pure geometry struct (MinimapRailMetrics) and a fixed-rect hit-test Shape (RailHitArea).

feature_notes: One tick per user message only. Replies, tool runs, notices and summaries never get ticks: .turn takes the first .user entry among its entries and returns nil if there is none; .group(.single(entry)) only when entry.item.content is .user; .group(.work), .group(.heads), .working, .merging and .headsWorking all return nil.
Tick title = the first 8 whitespace-separated words of the message text, with a single ellipsis character appended when the message has more than 8 words (firstWords(_:limit: 8)).

Snippet = the message text with every whitespace run collapsed to a single space, cut at 160 characters with an ellipsis appended when longer. The snippet is blanked to "" when it is empty or identical to the title, so short messages show only the title line in the card.
Tick weight = min(1, max(0.15, Double(text.count) / 420)): a message of 420 or more characters reaches full weight, and anything under 63 characters floors at 0.15.
Selection fallback: when the timeline reports no activeBlockID, the lit tick is the last outline block whose hasUserMessage is true.
Hovering alone only previews (sets hoveredID and mounts the card); only a press navigates.

Scrub gesture is DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local). .onChanged sets isPressing = true and calls onNavigate(id, false) each time the entry under the pointer changes, so the timeline tracks 1:1 unanimated; .onEnded sets isPressing = false and calls onNavigate(id, true) for one animated glide to the landing block. A zero-distance press therefore reads as a tap that jumps with animation.
Spacing: roomySpacing 8 when count*2 + (count-1)*8 fits in centerHeight; otherwise spacing = max(2, (height - count*2) / max(1, count-1)), tightening toward a 2 pt floor.

The tick stack is always vertically centred: topInset = (height - (ticks + gaps*spacing)) / 2, so a thread with more ticks than the rail can hold spills the same amount above and below instead of stacking against the top.

Y to entry mapping: raw = (y - topInset - tickHeight/2 + pitch/2) / pitch, rounded down and clamped to 0...count-1, where pitch = tickHeight + spacing = 2 + spacing. Inside the hit rect the area is solid, so a scrub never drops between ticks.

Hit rect: x 0, full rail width, from max(centerY(0) - pitch/2, Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight) to min(centerY(count-1) + pitch/2, railSize.height); .zero when count is 0 or bottom <= top. Ticks under the floating chrome row are veiled and take no pointer.
RailHitArea returns Path(rect) ignoring the bounds it is asked about, so the shape is the rect as computed and is not stretched to the rail's full column.

Live-resize behaviour: while WindowLiveResize.isActive the column renders lastEntries (the track scales in place and new user messages wait for the settle) and hoverAnimation is nil; the outline is rebuilt on the isActive true-to-false edge, on .onAppear, and on blocks changes when not resizing.

Render-cost isolation is deliberate and three-layered: TimelineMinimapColumn is Equatable so an unchanged blocks/tracking/centerHeight pass rebuilds nothing; MinimapSelection is the only view that observes TimelineScrollTracking so a scroll-visibility change re-runs just that small body; TimelineMinimapRail is used with .equatable() so a visibility change that moved nothing is skipped. The stated reason is that building titles in the timeline's own body re-rendered the whole conversation on every streamed token.

Ticks carry .animation(nil, value: centerHeight) so a height-only change (the rail's first layout at height 0, and window resizes) re-centres without sliding the whole stack down from the top on every thread opened.

Card height is estimated, never measured, to avoid a re-layout on every hover change: title 17 + padding 20 when there is no snippet; otherwise title 17 + 3 + lines*15 + 20, where glyphsPerLine = max(1, (300 - 24) / 7) = 39 and lines = min(3, max(1, ceil(snippet.count / 39))).
Cursor discipline: the pointing-hand cursor is pushed at most once (guarded by ownsCursorPush) and popped on hover .ended and on .onDisappear, so a view that disappears mid-hover pops exactly once.

centerHeight is the full chat-column height used only for centring; the rail's own frame stays timeline-height, so hit testing, scrubbing and the preview card never reach into the composer, and composer or queue-tab growth never shifts the ticks.

All code in this file is shipped: there are no #if DEBUG blocks, no feature flags and no dead branches; every declared symbol is reachable from TimelineMinimapColumn's body, the rail's gestures, or the accessibility actions.
