feature_notes: Hover controls are reserved inside the row (22pt) and then subtracted back out of its height with a negative bottom padding, so showing them never moves text and the gap between rows stays exactly 20pt: UserMessageRow uses minus (22 + 6) and AssistantMessageRow minus (22 + 2).

A user message whose text begins with ReplyQuote blocks shows those quotes as separate chips above the bubble so only the typed words stay in the bubble; each chip's help tooltip is the full quoted text and the excerpt is capped at 260pt wide on one line.

The edit pencil only appears when canRevert is true; it toggles runtime.messageEdit (a second tap closes the editor), and merely hovering it calls runtime.revertPreview so the click finds the preview done or nearly so.
Which message is open for editing lives on the thread runtime rather than the row, so leaving a thread only closes the popover and coming back reopens the editor on the same edit.

Right-clicking a user message opens a popover at the pointer with Copy message and Copy as markdown, plus Edit from here when revertable; the menu posts the intent through MessageMenuRequests.confirmRevert and the row then raises the confirmation dialog, so the AppKit menu never retains the row.

HydraReportRow pill summary reads 'Hank is done', 'Hank and Walter are done', 'Hank, Walter and Ada are done'; a head whose '## Name: task (failed)' or '(stopped)' section says otherwise is named with its outcome instead ('Walter failed'), and the whole summary goes through TextCleanup.singleLine with limit 140.
A note from Hydra itself (no heads listed) takes its first line as the pill title with one trailing full stop removed, and everything after that line as the popover body.

If a note body's first line is a bare http:// or https:// URL containing no whitespace, it becomes a sibling 'Open' link and is stripped from the details; if the rest parses as a HydraMergeNote against a MergeRequestLink the popover shows HydraMergePopover, otherwise plain markdown.

HydraHeadsWorkingRow shows only finished heads whose report has not reached the lead: a finished head is included when its batchID still has a running sibling, or, with no batch, when it finished at or after the earliest running head's startedAt; with no running heads at all the list is empty. It reads model.helpers(of: runtime.threadID) rather than scanning model.threads, so writes to other chats do not re-render it.

HydraShimmer sweeps a band across the text every 1.8 seconds at 30 frames per second, band width max(24, width / 3), gradient from Chrome.primaryText opacity 0 to 0.9 at the middle and back to 0; it is entirely absent when NSWorkspace reduce-motion is on and its TimelineView is paused while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling.

HydraBriefRow decides whether the head is still cooking from whether any other timeline entry shares the brief's turnID, memoized against runtime.entries.count so the scan runs once per count change rather than on every evaluation.

HydraDelegationBlock renders the lead's fenced hydra JSON as a card and never as JSON; it reads partial blocks as they stream through HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations and caches every reading in a 200-entry RecentCache keyed on the raw source string, so a finished block is the same card on every evaluation.
A delegation's project is displayed as just its last path component when the value contains a forward slash.

The merge pill is drawn under the outcome note's own id from the first stage onward, so the single row morphs (contents crossfade while the capsule glides to the new width) instead of being replaced; only the current state's contents take part in layout, drawn as a hidden sizing copy with the live contents overlaid and clipped.
A merging pill for a merge that is over (runtime.isHydraMerging false and no outcome note) removes itself rather than reading 'Merging...' forever.

The merge track's head hops: the arc is zero at every whole dot index and peaks half way between, so a jump over several dots arcs over each one in turn; when the merge is done every dot lights left to right as a wave and the head pops by 18 percent before settling to 18pt while the dots fade.
The merge flourish (track mode .done) fires only when the outcome title contains 'Hydra merged', and lasts 1100 milliseconds before the track falls to .resting.

Both the report pill and the merge pill call MarkdownView.warm off the main thread in a .task as they appear, so a tap finds blocks cached; for a heads' report each head's body is warmed separately from HydraReportDigest.parse(body).heads.

AttachmentThumbnail only mounts its AppKit anchor view after the pointer has hovered it, since a click always follows a hover; an 'anchorless' mode skips the anchor entirely so a strip can keep AppKit views out of SwiftUI's key-view-loop walk and the panel aims at the tap inside the strip's own anchor.
A thumbnail already shown is seeded from ThumbnailMemory in init, so scrolling back to it never fades it in again.

WorkGroup renders a single entry as a bare ToolRow with no header or chevron; a group the agent has moved past (reply text follows it) starts collapsed, and startsCollapsed turning true re-collapses it, but a group the reader opened is never closed on its own (the onChange is one-way).

WorkSteps shows only the last 2 entries and folds the rest behind an 'N earlier steps' line; expanding either a group or the fold calls the revealTimelineEnd action so the view scrolls to keep the end in sight.

ToolPresentation.label strips a leading word that only restates the kind, using per-kind root lists: command [run, bash, shell, exec, execute, command], read [read, view, open, cat], edit [edit, write, multiedit, create, notebookedit, apply_patch, patch], search [search, grep, glob, find], web [fetch, webfetch, websearch, browse], mcp [call], agent [delegate, agent, task], other [use]. So a call titled 'Edit file' reads 'Edited file' rather than 'Edited Edit file'.
MCP calls are recognized by a title of the form '<server> \u00b7 <tool>' (space, middle dot, space) resolved through MCPCatalog.entry(matching:); the label renders as '<entry.name>: <tool>'.

A tool row with non-empty edit paths opens the diff popover; a read with a resolvable image (or any row with an image and no other output) opens the image panel; otherwise a row with output or detail expands inline. A call with none of those renders as a plain line of text rather than a control, so the pointer and VoiceOver treat it as text.

A delegation call whose head thread is not yet linked reads its own title: 'Pip: the merge popover' names the roster persona and the task; otherwise the team's first face stands in and the row says 'a head'. Titles in the set {subagent, agent, task, empty} are treated as the tool's own word for itself and produce no task, so the row never reads 'Delegating Subagent'.

HydraHeadStepsPopover filters the head's entries: the first user message (the brief, shown above) is dropped, later briefs are kept as the lead steering the head on, blank replies are dropped, tool calls and notices are always kept, and reasoning, turnEnd, plan and todos are dropped as the head's own bookkeeping.

Tool output is collapsed to the first 30 lines, counted by scanning the UTF-8 bytes for newline (0x0A) rather than splitting the whole output, because a running command's row re-renders on every flush; the expand button reports the full line count.
Diffs in expanded tool rows are parsed once per distinct (path, diff) pair into a 60-entry RecentCache, so opening and closing a row is instant no matter how large the patch is.

A turn's conclusive answer is defined as the replies that follow its last tool call: reaching for a tool clears the collected answer entries, while plans, notices and checklists do not. A turn that ended on a tool (stopped or failed mid-work) falls back to the last reply it made.
In a collapsed turn, plans and non-info notices stay visible so a failed turn never hides what went wrong; plain info notices only appear when the turn is expanded.
TurnFinishedBlock opens expanded when the chronological timeline setting is on, and folded otherwise; either way the chevron toggles between the answer and the full steps.

TurnFinishedBlock memoizes everything it derives from a turn against a key of the content entries' ObjectIdentifiers plus the expanded flag, and writes the cache in an onChange rather than in the body.

For older turns whose summary carries no changes, the block computes them once through runtime.parsedDiff(selection: turnID) and writes them back with runtime.storeLegacyChanges, guarded on summary.filesChanged > 0 or derived.hasEdits and on Task.isCancelled.

The heads a turn sent out are always listed below the response, folded or not, and are explicitly excluded from the expanded steps (TimelineGroup .heads cases are filtered out) so a head never disappears with the steps.
TurnFileCard's Review button only mounts its NSView anchor after the pointer has hovered it, since a folded turn is a block of a lazy stack and the anchor is only ever needed for a click.
unresolved_questions: HydraMergeRow.mergingContent and mergingLabel are documented as 'the spinner, the stage with its shimmer, the time', but the shipped code draws only the stage Text inside HStack(spacing: 8): the spinner and the elapsed clock were removed and the doc comments left stale. Whether the spinner is expected back cannot be told from this file.
ToolPresentation.mcpLabel(entry:tool:running:) accepts a running flag it never uses, so the label is tense-invariant; whether callers expect a running form is not determinable here.
HydraDelegationBlock's sent flag defaults to false and is set by a caller outside this file, so which timeline code passes sent: true, and at what moment, is unknown from here.

TimelineMetrics.hoverLineHeight (22) is still reserved on both message rows, but the comments say it is kept 'with no copy button left to size it'; whether anything else is meant to occupy that line is not established in this file.
The asset catalog image named badge-edit used by TurnFileCard is not in this file, so its artwork and pixel dimensions are unknown here.

HydraMergeRow indexes the track with runtime.hydraMergeStep?.rawValue against HydraMergeStage.allCases.count; the enum's raw values and their ordering are defined elsewhere and are assumed to be zero-based and contiguous.

FinishedHeadPill composes its visible text from HydraNameStyle.text plus a literal suffix while building a separate title string for the accessibility label; whether the two can diverge for a status outside failed/stopped/completed is not testable from this file alone.
HydraShimmer is applied only to HydraBriefRow's cooking title and to HydraMergeRow's stage words within this file; whether other callers exist is outside this bundle.

feature_notes: ModelCatalog.entries: when settings.modelList is empty it offers every available provider's models; otherwise exactly the pinned list, resolved through registry.model(pin.modelID, for: pin.provider). The thread's current model is inserted at index 0 if it is not already in the list, so a chat never loses its own model.
Chip tapping opens a 330-wide popover showing the slider; the slider's title opens the model list in the same popover; the list's chevron.left returns.

Choosing a model row: switching provider clears providerSessionID and providerResumeAt and stops the existing runtime session; effort is taken from the saved ModelPreference only if the new model still lists it; fastMode = option.supportsFast && preference.fastMode; the chat leaves any Hydra pair (leaveHydraPair); settings.defaultProvider is set to the chosen provider.
Choosing a pair row calls model.enterHydraPair and dismisses the whole popover; tapping the pair the chat is already in re-settles model, effort and Hydra.
Reset button: effort goes to the pair's orchestratorEffort when in a pair and that effort still exists on the model, otherwise nil (the model default); fastMode goes to false.
Every slider/fast-mode change is remembered as that model's setting for future chats (setPreference + remember).
hasHistory locks cross-provider rows with the detail string "New chats only".
Effort resolution order in the card: thread.effort, then defaultEffort, then the index of "medium", then 0.

Title colour rules: in a pair a gradient [lead titleColor] + pair.brand.titleColors (+ EffortPalette.fast appended in fast mode); else max+fast = gradient brand.titleColor -> EffortPalette.fast, max alone = brand.title, fast alone = EffortPalette.fast, neither = EffortPalette.title.

TrackEffect traits: particles count = max(10, width/5), streaks count = max(5, width/14). Particle: height random(seed,1), speed 12 + 28*r, radius 0.7 + 1.1*r, start r, brightness 0.22 + 0.5*r, shimmerRate 2 + 3*r (seed = index). Streak: length 10 + 20*r, speed 110 + 190*r, thickness 1.1 + 1.1*r, start r, height 0.2 + 0.6*r, brightness 0.35 + 0.55*r (seed = index + 100).
drawParticles: span = width + 8, y = height * (0.16 + 0.68 * particle.height), shimmer = 0.6 + 0.4*sin(time*rate + index), skipped under opacity 0.01, drawn as filled circles.

drawStreaks: span = width + length + 12, x offset -length - 6, rounded rect of height = thickness with cornerRadius thickness/2, filled with a white gradient from opacity 0 to brightness left-to-right; skipped under brightness 0.02.

drawBolts: exactly 2 slots, seed = slot + 200, period 1.4 + 0.9*r, flash window 0.26 s, intensity = sin(phase/0.26 * pi); x = 12 + (width-24)*r(cycleSeed,3) with cycleSeed = seed + cycle*7.31, lean 3.0 + 3.0*r; zigzag path from (x+lean, 3) to (x-lean*0.4, h*0.42) to (x+lean*0.5, h*0.5) to (x-lean, h-3); glow stroke blur 3, EffortPalette.fast.opacity(0.9*intensity), lineWidth 4 round; core stroke white.opacity(intensity) lineWidth 1.5.
drawSheen: band 46 points, period 2.8 s, slanted quad leaning 10 points, gradient white/spark 0 -> 0.22 -> 0.

drawFusion: seam x = width * (0.5 + 0.13*sin(t*0.7) + 0.05*sin(t*1.9 + 1)); pulse = 0.5 + 0.5*sin(t*2.4); gradient stops lead at 0 and at seam/width - 0.22, white.opacity(0.92) at the seam, heads colours from seam/width + 0.16 to 1. Three plasma bands (seed = band + 300) drawn twice (toward each side) with blendMode .plusLighter, blur 2.5, clipped to their side, reach = width*0.55, brightness 0.32 + 0.16*r, amplitude height*(0.12 + 0.16*r), wavelength 30 + 34*r, speed 22 + 34*r, thickness 1.8 + 2.2*r, sampled every 3 points. 22 sparks (seed = index + 400), life 0.7 + 0.8*r, speed 28 + 74*r, radius 0.7 + 1.5*(1-progress), y wobble 5*sin(age*8 + seed), colour white mixed toward the landing side by progress*0.8. Seam core: plusLighter blur 7 ellipse of half-width 9 + 8*pulse spanning -h*0.2 to 1.4h at white.opacity(0.32 + 0.3*pulse), plus a blur-0.8 rounded rect 2.2 wide, inset 2 top and bottom, cornerRadius 1.1, white.opacity(0.5 + 0.4*pulse); then drawSheen in white.

edgeFade fades over the last 14 points at either end; random(index, trait) = fract(sin(index*12.9898 + trait*78.233) * 43758.5453), the classic GLSL hash, marked nonisolated so trait building is off the main actor.
Frame rate: TimelineView minimumInterval 1/30 only for kind == .supercharged with no pair, otherwise 1/60; paused when reduceMotion is on or the window is not visible (FrontMonitor.shared.isVisible).

WebsiteCaptures hooks are compiled in but gated on WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled and only on the non-compact chip; they record the chip's NSView anchor and its global frame per thread id for marketing captures.

feature_notes: Rows are sent as direct user chat messages once the running turn finishes, top to bottom.

cappedHeight: once count > maxRows (7) and heights are known, height = (listHeight - sum(rowHeights)) + 7 * average row height, so the cut always lands on a whole row; below the cap the natural listHeight stands.
numbers(for:): one shared number per bundle - the counter only climbs when a prompt has no bundleID or starts a new bundle, so a bundled pair shows one number and a link glyph.

Reorder maths: only vertical travel counts (translation.height); the translation is applied inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true; RowDrag.settle uses fallbackHeight 32 and pastCentre = pairBand = 0.25, and swaps run inside .spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82).

Pairing: the target is the neighbour in the direction of travel when |abs(offset) - (ownHeight + slotHeight)/2| <= slotHeight * 0.25; the held row indents 14 points to the right while a pair target is live.
Dragging a bundled row more than 0.6 of its own height out of its slot unbundles it (levelChange haptic); hovering the neighbour's middle again re-pairs on release.

Release with a pair target calls runtime.bundleFollowUp(held, onto: target) inside .spring(response: 0.36, dampingFraction: 0.78), then the drag settles with .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8).
A row removed mid-drag (sent or deleted) ends the drag cleanly and its measured height is pruned from rowHeights.
The whole title line toggles the fold; the chevron only indicates direction.

Every control in the tab is .focusable(false) on purpose: the key-view-loop builder spun the main thread forever when the collapse button sat flush above a trash button at the same x (documented as the Sept 15 2026 freezes).
RowHeightReporter is always applied, never switched in when a drag starts, because changing a row's structure mid-gesture tore the gesture down and left the row lifted for good.
The pencil toggles: a second tap while the editor is open sets runtime.followUpEdit = nil and closes it.
The editor and the attachment preview both hang from window rects (windowRectAnchor) rather than mounting an AppKit anchor view, to keep AppKit views out of this tab entirely.

feature_notes: The rendered state is `fused = isFused || !animates`, so rows that pass animates: false draw the mark at rest immediately.
gradient(lead:heads:): lead colours spread across locations 0 to 0.42 and heads colours across 0.58 to 1, so each half wears its own brand and blending happens only across the hairline.

When heads == lead, the heads' colour is a lighter shade of the lead's own: titleColor.opacity(0.55) for a light (silver) brand, otherwise titleColor.mix(with: .white, by: 0.4) - one model over its smaller self.
brandColors: the antigravity brand expands to the three-colour EffortBrand.gemini sweep; every other brand contributes just its titleColor.
spread(): a single colour is emitted as two stops at start and end (a flat band); several colours are laid evenly with location = start + (end-start) * index / (count-1).
The appear animation is retriggered by the .task id, so changing either provider replays the fusion.
unresolved_questions: ProviderKind.iconName maps to asset-catalogue image names that are not visible from this file, so the exact artwork of each half is not determinable here.
The 30 ms sleep before animating is presumably to let the view settle before the spring starts; the file does not state the reason.

feature_notes: Reload trigger: .task(id: loadKey) where loadKey is "<runtime.diffRevision>-<diffSelection uuid or 'all'>-<diffFocusRevision>", so a new turn, a different turn selection, or a new focus request reloads the panel.
Opening latency rule: when runtime.hasCachedDiff(selection:) is false the view sleeps 180 ms and bails if cancelled before calling load(); an already-parsed diff loads with no delay.

focusedFiles(): for each FileEdit with a non-empty path and a non-empty .diff patch that is not already covered (TouchedPaths.matches) by the parsed diff or by an earlier missing entry, DiffParser.parseHunks builds a DiffFile and it is kept only if hunks are non-empty; results are prepended (files = missing + parsed). This makes a tapped tool row always show its edit even when the turn is still running, or the work was reverted or moved into a worktree.

After load: collapse state is decided in three branches. (1) If any file matches the focus paths, collapsed = all ids minus the focused ones, scrollTarget = the first focused id, scrollRequest += 1, which animates a 0.25 s smooth scrollTo(anchor: .top) on the next main-queue hop. (2) Else if files.count > 6 and collapsed is empty, every file but the first is collapsed. (3) Else the previous collapsed set is intersected with the current file ids.
Per-file render budget: 200 lines (collapsedLineLimit) until 'Show all' is tapped, then Int.max; the budget is spent across hunks, so a huge hunk only materializes its first 200 lines.

Tinted runs merge across hunk boundaries and are emitted in chunks of 40 rows (tintedChunk), each chunk carrying the run's absolute offset and total count so corner rounding is computed against the whole merged run; a hunk header that would land inside a continuing run is dropped (continues = first run isTinted and pending non-empty).

Equatable conformances are explicit render optimizations. DiffFileCard == compares file.id, additions, deletions, hunks.count, change, isBinary and isCollapsed. DiffLinesView == compares sectionsKey and showsLineNumbers, so a sibling card's collapse never rebuilds these rows but the same path with a different line count does.

Sections are computed twice on purpose: inline in body as a fallback when @State sections is empty (so a card materialized mid-scroll draws rows on its first frame) and in .onChange(of: "<sectionsKey>|<showsAll>", initial: true).

Container choice: when showsAll and totalLines > 200 the rows go in a LazyVStack; otherwise a VStack with .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true) so the panel's outer LazyVStack gets exact card heights and no row is dropped while scrolling.

DiffPopoverCoordinator.sync three cases: (1) a different runtime - close, clear the previous runtime's isDiffVisible, adopt the new runtime, seed seenOpenRequest from its diffOpenRequest, and outside a capture run force isDiffVisible = false so the diff never auto-opens after a thread switch, then return; (2) first adoption (runtime == nil) - same seeding, and if isVisible outside a capture run clear the flag and return; (3) same runtime - desiredVisible = isVisible then show() or close().

reopen(runtime:) opens only for the runtime already served (otherwise it delegates to sync) and only when diffOpenRequest differs from seenOpenRequest; if the popover is already shown on the same resolved anchor view it is a no-op, otherwise monitors stop, session/pendingSession bump, popover.close(), then show() on the new anchor.

Anchor resolution order in resolvedAnchor(): runtime.diffAnchor?.value with a non-nil window paired with runtime.diffAnchorEdge (a tool row opens below itself, a Review button above itself), else the first of [tab anchor, composer fallback] whose window is non-nil, with edge .maxY.

show() guards on a resolved anchor and on the popover not already being shown, bumps session, installs the fixed content DiffInspector(runtime:) at 640x540, starts the monitors, records shownOn/shownRuntime and shows relative to target.view.bounds.

Stale-close guard: popoverDidClose hops to @MainActor, stops monitors, clears desiredVisible, and only when session == pendingSession clears the shown runtime's isDiffVisible and sets popover.contentViewController = nil (releasing the inspector so it stops observing the runtime off screen); shownRuntime is always cleared.

Dismissal behavior: a left or right mouse-down whose window is not the popover's content window closes the popover but the event is still returned so it reaches its target (picking another turn's Review opens that diff in one tap); mouse-downs inside the popover pass through unchanged; Escape (keyCode 53) closes and swallows the event (returns nil).
Documented close paths in the coordinator's doc comment: Escape, the X button, Command-D, tapping the changes tab, or the thread going away.

Shipped vs capture-only: the !WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled guards are live in normal launches (they suppress auto-opening after a thread switch); only under --website-captures or --tour-captures is a pre-set isDiffVisible preserved so scripted captures can show the diff popover open.

The default value of runtime.diffAnchorEdge and the code that sets diffAnchor / bumps diffOpenRequest live in ThreadRuntime, outside this bundle.

feature_notes: Rows are rebuilt only when ResultsKey changes (query, model.threads, model.projects, model.selectedThreadID, model.finishActionTitle) with initial: true, so arrow-key movement and hover selection never recompute the list.
onAppear sets isFocused = true so the search field takes focus as soon as the palette appears; onChange(of: query) resets selection to 0.

Up arrow: selection = max(0, selection - 1). Down arrow: selection = min(max(0, items.count - 1), selection + 1). Both return .handled, so the clamp never runs past the ends. Escape calls close() and returns .handled. Return (onSubmit) runs the selected row.
Hovering a row sets selection to that index, deliberately so the pointer and the arrow keys never disagree about what Return will run; tapping a row sets selection then runs it.
run(_:) guards items.indices.contains(selection), calls close() FIRST and only then item.perform(), so the palette is always dismissed before the action fires.
close() only sets model.isCommandPalettePresented = false; tapping the scrim and pressing Escape both route through it.

Base action set, always present, in this order: new-thread ("New thread", square.and.pencil, ShortcutStore.label(for: .newThread), model.newThread()); new-worktree ("New thread in worktree", arrow.triangle.branch, .newWorktreeThread, model.newThread(workspace: .worktree)); add-project ("Add project", folder.badge.plus, .addProject, model.chooseProjectFolder()).

Thread-dependent actions are appended only when model.selectedThreadID is non-nil: terminal ("Toggle terminal", terminal, .toggleTerminal, runtime.isTerminalVisible.toggle()); changes ("Toggle changes", plusminus, .toggleChanges, runtime.toggleDiff()); finish (title model.finishActionTitle, symbol model.finishActionSymbol, .finishThread, model.finishSelectedThread()).
settings ("Settings", gearshape, .openSettings, WindowManager.shared.showSettings()) is appended last and is always present, after the conditional thread actions.
needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased(). Actions are filtered by title.lowercased().contains(needle) only when the needle is non-empty; with an empty needle all actions pass.

Thread rows drop isArchived and isInPanel threads, match on title.lowercased().contains(needle), sort by updatedAt descending, and take prefix(6) with an empty query or prefix(10) while searching. Subtitle is model.project(thread.projectID)?.name, symbol "bubble.left", id is thread.id.uuidString, and running it sets model.selectedThreadID = thread.id.

Project rows are suppressed entirely when the query is empty; otherwise every project whose name.lowercased() contains the needle becomes a row with id project.id.uuidString calling model.newThread(in: project).

Ordering differs by mode: with an empty query the list is Array(threads) + matchingActions (recent threads first); with a non-empty query it is matchingActions + Array(threads) + projects. The combined list is then truncated with prefix(12).
Shortcut labels come from ShortcutStore rather than hard-coded strings, so a remapped chord shows the new keys and a cleared chord shows no shortcut text at all.
The empty-results branch never leaves a blank box: it renders the single-line Nothing matches message with the query echoed inside curly quotes and middle truncation.

FloatingSidebarPanel receives canClose: !onlyFloats, so in only-floating mode it cannot be dismissed.

Sidebar rows are laid out once at sidebar.width and the slide animates only the outer clip frame (renderedWidth), so rows do not re-wrap per frame; sidebar.noteLaidOutWidth is fed from onGeometryChange of the inner width.

The detail pane is .clipped() deliberately: ReserveSlide offsets carrying a conversation sideways, panels settling after a pane resize, and rows re-wrapping in a live resize otherwise drew over the sidebar or past the window edge for a few frames.
Leading padding on the detail pane is 0 when the sidebar is visible and not only-floating, otherwise Chrome.sheetInset; trailing and vertical padding are always Chrome.sheetInset.

The backdrop is painted first and the whole stack is then clipped to RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Chrome.windowCornerRadius, style: .continuous), so the glass and its edge stop at the window's own curve.
A coordinate space named GenieAnimator.coordinateSpace is established at the root and used by the GenieLayer and RowGlideLayer overlays.

Drag and drop anywhere in the window (dropDestination for URL.self): directories become projects (one model.addProject per folder), a new thread opens in the last added project, and plain files are attached to the selected thread's draft via Storage.attach(files.map(AttachmentSource.file), to: ...draft.attachments); URLs that do not exist on disk are skipped; handleDrop returns true only if at least one folder or file was accepted.
Alerts are a single OK button with role .cancel, driven by model.alert being non-nil; dismissing writes model.alert = nil.

Chat columns are cached AppKit hosting views, not rebuilt SwiftUI subtrees: Coordinator.keptLimit = 8 columns stay built behind the shown one (while order.count > keptLimit + 1, drop order[0]), because rebuilding a long thread's rows cost about a quarter of a second each switch.

Hidden columns keep the frame they were built at and autoresizingMask [], so a sidebar slide or live resize does not relayout them; the shown column takes pane.bounds with autoresizingMask [.width, .height] and isHidden = false.

show(_:) is a no-op when the id is already shown; otherwise the previous column is hidden, its autoresizingMask cleared and its rootView rebuilt with isShown: false before the new one is revealed or made.

Columns are dropped in dropHidden when their thread has a turn running (the running set), the thread no longer exists (model.thread == nil) or there is no existing runtime, so a hidden column never streams rows unseen at full cost.

Prebuild policy in DetailView: after selecting a thread wait 1500 ms, then build model.neighbors(of: threadID) one at a time; on the first pass of a launch also append the first ThreadColumns.topRowsBuiltAtLaunch = 6 of model.sidebarThreads. Before each build it waits while the last input event is younger than 1 second, polling every 300 ms, and returns entirely if the selected thread starts running; 400 ms between builds.
A prebuilt column is inserted at order index 0 so it is the first evicted, ahead of the columns the reader actually visited.
requested = Set(ids) after each prebuild pass, so a column dropped to make room is not rebuilt on every SwiftUI update.

Dropped columns go into retired and are removed from their superview by a Task 500 ms later, keeping teardown off the switch frame; the retirement Task is cancelled and restarted by each drop and guards on !Task.isCancelled.

Each column's root view is AnyView(ChatView(runtime: model.runtime(for: id)).environment(\.chatColumnIsShown, isShown).modifier(HostedEnvironment(model: model, liveResize: liveResize))); the chatColumnIsShown environment value (default true) is how a view inside a column learns whether it is the visible one, replacing onAppear/onDisappear which would fire for hidden columns.
Columns are hidden rather than detached because a hosting view removed from the window looks disappeared to its views and every task in the column restarts when it returns.
SwitchLatency.note logs "prebuilt <first 24 characters of the thread title, or ?> in <ContinuousClock duration>" for each prebuild.

The Welcome empty state appears only when model.projects.isEmpty; with projects but no selected thread, NoThreadView shows instead. The same branch also runs when the selected thread id no longer resolves to a thread.
NoThreadView reads the live New Thread chord from ShortcutStore.label(for: .newThread) so a remapped shortcut never leaves a stale key on screen; the label is simply omitted when nil.

Provider rows: API-key-based providers never show Install or Login; both the not-installed and the signed-out case show "Add key", which opens Settings and navigates to the Providers page rather than sending the reader to a web page.

CopyCommandButton shows the command text itself and flips to a checkmark plus "Copied" for 1.4 seconds before reverting, matching the transcript's copy button; it previously stayed on "Copied" for the rest of the launch.

feature_notes: Notes parsing recognizes headings 'new features'/'new' -> New, 'bug fixes'/'fixes'/'bugs' -> Bugs, 'refinements'/'improvements' -> Refinements, case-insensitively, bare or wrapped in #-heading or **bold** chrome, with trailing ':' stripped
Bullet markers accepted: '-', U+2010, U+2013, U+2014, U+2212, '*', '•', each followed by a space or tab
Lines that are empty, '---', or start with '<' are skipped entirely
Any other heading (for example 'Thanks to contributors') closes the current section so its bullets are dropped
Bullets are de-duplicated case-insensitively per section, keeping the first occurrence

A last bullet containing the word 'extra' preceded by a number becomes the section's rollup, its number counts toward changeCount but it renders in the tertiary style below the bullets (example shape: "Fixed 12 extra issues…")
Inline Markdown stripped from bullets: [text](url) -> text, **text** -> text, `text` -> text, then whitespace trimmed
Notes in any other shape produce an empty digest and the page falls back to rendering the raw notes as Markdown
parse(_:) memoizes on the raw string so re-evaluations of the About page do not re-run three regexes per bullet

The progress head only moves forward: a lower target snaps down immediately, a higher one is chased exponentially with dt clamped to 0.25s, step at least minimumSpeed*dt, and snaps once within 0.0001 of the target
Chase response: 0.15 under reduceMotion, 0.72 while phase == .celebrating, otherwise 0.3; minimumSpeed 0.12 while celebrating else 0
Frame clock pauses when the head is settled or while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling; the sparkle canvas also pauses when sparkles are empty

The pill shows the slider whenever progress.showsProgressUI, otherwise the Update & restart button when checker.updateAvailable && checker.update != nil && !showsProgressUI, otherwise the standing seal
The seal distinguishes 'Check failed' (lastError != nil) and 'Not checked yet' (lastCheckedAt == nil) from 'Up to date', so it no longer claims up-to-date before a successful check
Opening the About page runs checker.check(); if progress.consumePendingCelebration() is true it runs the post-relaunch sweep

Celebration sweep: sleep 550ms, bail unless phase == .celebrating, finishCelebrationSweep(), then under reduceMotion one .alignment haptic + 900ms, else 900ms, .alignment haptic, 450ms, .levelChange haptic, 700ms, then completeCelebration()
Leaving the page mid-sweep cancels the task and calls completeCelebration() so the pill lands on Up to date immediately
Release detail joins with " · ": "Released <long date>", the file-style byte count, and always "Update & restart installs it in place and relaunches."

Check row detail: "Asking GitLab for the latest release…" while checking; otherwise "<error> Checked <relative>." on error, "Droppy Code <version> is ready to install. Checked <relative>." when an update waits, else "Droppy Code checks GitLab for new versions a few times a day. Checked <relative>."; when never checked the suffix is "Not checked yet."
Update distribution is GitLab releases of a signed and notarized disk image

feature_notes: Connection celebration: when model.mcp.states flips an id to connected, the id is inserted into `celebrating`, SettleChime.play() fires, and after a 900ms Task.sleep it is removed, so the card flashes success in the grid and then moves to the 'Connected' section. The whole block is guarded by `guard !reduceMotion else { return }`, so with Reduce Motion the card moves straight across with no flash and no chime.
Grid animation: .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35), value: celebrating) with .transition(.scale(scale: 0.9).combined(with: .opacity)) on each card.
Search matching is case-insensitive over entry.name, entry.vendor, entry.summary, entry.id and any sampleTools element; an empty or whitespace-only query matches everything.
The Custom section hides itself completely while searching when no custom server matches; when not searching it always shows, with the explainer row when the user has none.

Connect flow (identical in MCPServerCard.begin() and MCPCustomRow.begin()): `!entry.needsInput` connects immediately via model.mcp.connect(entry); otherwise MCPKeyPanel.shared.present takes the field values.
A card whose state becomes .needsSetup auto-presents MCPSetupPanel with no user action, because the user just came back from the browser expecting a result.

Custom editor save(): builds `draft`; records wasConnected; model.mcp.saveCustom(draft, replacing: server?.id ?? savedID) and on failure sets error = failure.message and returns; sets savedID = draft.id; writes values with saveCustomValues(keptValues, for: draft.id, replacingFieldsOf: server?.catalogEntry()) and on failure shows the literal 'The Keychain could not save a value. Keep this editor open and try again.'; if it was connected and model.mcp.entry(for: draft.id) resolves, calls refresh; then dismiss().
savedID exists so a retry after a failed first save replaces the record just created rather than adding a duplicate.

Argument parsing: argsText is split on newline, lines that are whitespace-only after trimming are dropped, but surviving lines are NOT trimmed, so a leading dash, embedded spaces or quotes reach the server exactly as typed.
Variable keys are trimmed with .whitespaces; rows whose key is empty are dropped silently in both `draft` and `keptValues` rather than failing validation.
Switching kind preserves the variable list: the same keys become env vars for stdio or headers for http.

Editing pre-loads stored values on appear via model.mcp.storedValue(server:field:secret:); name focus is taken only when adding (server == nil), never when editing, so it does not read as a prompt to rename.
VariableDraft's identity is a UUID, deliberately not the key, because the key changes on every keystroke and would throw the row out of the ForEach mid-edit.

Hover info button: opens 220ms after the pointer arrives and closes 320ms after it has left BOTH the button and the popover, so the gap between them can be crossed; clicking cancels the pending settle and toggles immediately.
The tools popover and the custom edit popover are attached to the ellipsis button rather than the row, deliberately, because hung from the row they opened from the row's middle.
Connected rows are sorted alphabetically by entry.name; grid section order follows MCPCatalog.byCategory.
MCPCustomRow shows the SettingsSwitch only in the .connected state, whereas MCPConnectedRow shows it always (it only exists for connected entries).

isPresenting(entry) guards re-entry: if the same entry's panel is already visible, present() only calls orderFrontRegardless and returns, so a failing re-check never reopens the browser page or rebuilds the steps under the user.
The NSPanel instance is reused across entries (`self.panel ?? makePanel()`); only contentViewController and size are replaced, and the escape monitor is installed at most once.
Escape (keyCode 53) closes the panel and the key event is consumed (the monitor returns nil).
Traffic lights are hidden deliberately because there is no title bar to hold them; closing is via the xmark button or Escape.
Pressing the guide.pageLabel button re-opens guide.pageURL in the browser.
'Check again' sets checkedOnce = true and calls model.mcp.refresh(entry); the follow-up status line only renders when checkedOnce is true and the probe is not currently connecting.
On connection the body swaps to successView and .onChange(of: state.isConnected) schedules onDone() 1.2 seconds later, which closes the panel.
Under accessibilityReduceMotion the success checkmark is set to full scale immediately rather than springing; unlike MCPServerCard, this view still shows the success state.
onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } reports the content height to MCPSetupPanel.shared.fit, so the panel follows content growth (the status line, the success view).
The whole background is a WindowDragArea, so a press anywhere the controls do not claim (reason text, steps, status line) drags the panel clear of the browser page behind it.

feature_notes: Filtering is deliberately instant with NO transitions: the comment records that animating dozens of rows with blur on every keystroke (and again on clearing) made entries overlap and jump.
matches() tests shortName, name, detail, the raw model id and provider.displayName with localizedCaseInsensitiveContains; an empty query matches everything.

The pinned list uses a plain VStack, not the card's lazy stack, on purpose: a lazy stack rebuilds a row that changes slot and animates it in from the container origin (sending the grabbed row flying to the top) and also ignores zIndex, which the lifted row needs.

Drag reorder: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 1, coordinateSpace: .global) on the grip only; the translation is applied inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true so the grabbed row tracks the pointer exactly, while neighbour swaps animate with .spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82).

The visible order is recomputed on every move via visiblePins(query:) rather than captured in the gesture, so swaps happen against the currently visible neighbour and hidden (filtered-out) models keep their relative place through settings.moveModel(pin, to: neighbour, placeAfter:).
RowDrag.settle is passed fallbackHeight: 54 for rows whose height has not been measured yet.
A landed swap fires NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment at .now.
Drag end animates drag back to a fresh RowDrag() with .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8) and pops the closed-hand cursor; it returns early when drag.id is nil.

Cursor bookkeeping: the open-hand push is popped on the grip's onDisappear and on isDragged going false while the pointer is not over the grip, covering the case where the drag is released away from the grip with no leave event.
rowHeights is pruned in .onChange(of: pins) whenever the dictionary holds more entries than pins, so an unpinned model takes its measured height with it.
Adding to and removing from the picker animate with Chrome.panelSlide.
Each ProviderModelsSection runs `.task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) }`, so catalogs load lazily as sections appear; the 'Load models' button forces a reload with force: true.
A provider section is listed only when the trimmed query is empty or at least one of its models matches the query.
The whole 'Your models' section is skipped when a search matches none of the pinned models (`trimmed.isEmpty || !visiblePins.isEmpty`).

The effort and fast-mode bindings read and write through settings.preference/setPreference on every get and set rather than holding local copies, so the popover always reflects stored state; onReset writes a default ModelPreference().

purpose: A small @MainActor @Observable object that tracks whether a settings pane is being scrolled right now, reports that to the global ScrollActivity under one fixed pane UUID so effects that should not run under a moving finger rest, and exposes a separate isFrozen flag that tells settings rows to stop hovering and animating while content slides under the pointer.
state_owned: isScrolling: Bool (observable, private setter)
isFrozen: Bool (observable, private setter)
isCoasting: Bool (@ObservationIgnored)
settle: Task<Void, Never>? (@ObservationIgnored, the debounce task)
side_effects: Registers and unregisters with the global ScrollActivity.shared singleton under the fixed pane UUID
Spawns a @MainActor Task that sleeps 150 milliseconds as the settle debounce, cancelling the previous one on each note()
platform_assumptions: Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) and @MainActor isolation
Structured concurrency with Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(150)) and Task.isCancelled
Assumes a caller that can distinguish an active drag or wheel movement from a coasting flick, which on macOS comes from NSEvent scroll phase and momentum phase
ui_elements: No views: it drives row hover suppression through isFrozen and effect pausing through isScrolling elsewhere
feature_notes: note() is documented as 'a frame of movement': the first call flips isScrolling true and calls ScrollActivity.shared.setScrolling(true, timeline: Self.pane, reporter: self); every call restarts a 150ms debounce, after which isScrolling and isCoasting go false, isFrozen is cleared if set, and ScrollActivity is told scrolling stopped.
isFrozen is raised in note() only when `!isCoasting && !isFrozen`, so once the flick is coasting, further momentum frames do not re-freeze the rows.
coast() sets isCoasting = true and clears isFrozen immediately, so a click that stops a flick always reaches its target; the comment names this 'the chat timeline's rule'.
end() cancels the settle task, sets it to nil, clears isFrozen and isCoasting, then `guard isScrolling else { return }` so it only reports scrolling stopped when it had reported it started.
The pane key is a single `private static let pane = UUID()` shared by every instance, so all settings panes report under one timeline id rather than one per instance.
The settle task guards `guard let self, !Task.isCancelled else { return }` before mutating state, and captures self weakly.
unresolved_questions: The callers of note(), coast() and end() are not in this file, so which NSEvent phases map to coast() versus note() cannot be confirmed here.
ScrollActivity.shared's semantics - what pauses when a timeline reports scrolling and what the `reporter:` argument is used for - are defined elsewhere.
Whether isFrozen is consumed by every settings row or only some is not determinable from this file.

launch() refuses when from.width <= 1 or from.height <= 1, and refuses entirely when Reduce Motion is enabled
launch() removes any existing glide for the same threadID before appending, so a thread has at most one ghost in the air
A launch is aimed at a fallback rect just past the list's edge, so if the new row never reports a frame the ghost slips out under the clip instead of landing

land() re-targets a glide only when the glide exists, is younger than the 0.5 second landingWindow, and its direction matches the settled flag; the latest report inside the window wins and the interpolation absorbs the re-targeting
Per-thread ObservedValue<Bool> hiding cells mean a launch, landing or finish re-renders only the two rows of that glide plus the layer, not every row in the list
setHiding writes only when the value actually changes, so a row is never re-rendered for a write that said what it already showed
arrive() runs at settlingDuration - 0.12 seconds and un-hides the real row so it shows under the ghost's last frames; finish() removes the ghost 0.12 seconds later, so the handover never shows a gap
finish() re-derives hiding as glides.contains { $0.threadID == threadID && !$0.hasArrived }, so a thread relaunched meanwhile stays hidden
Geometry interpolates x, y, width and height linearly in the spring-driven progress p, so the ghost resizes as well as moves between the two row frames
lift = min(smoothstep(0, 0.12, p), 1 - smoothstep(0.7, 1, p)): the row lifts within the first 12 percent of the flight and has set back down through the last 30 percent
fill = max(departureFill + (arrivalFill - departureFill) * p, 0.12 * lift), so an unfilled row still shows a faint plate at up to 0.12 while airborne
smoothstep is t * t * (3 - 2 * t) with t = (x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0) clamped to 0...1
The keyframe track is a single SpringKeyframe(1.0, spring: RowGlideAnimator.spring) from an initial value of 0.0, triggered by hasStarted flipping true in onAppear
render() snapshots any Face view at the given size, aligned .topLeading, with the colorScheme forced into the environment so a ghost matches the theme it was captured in
hasLanded is set by land() but is never read anywhere in this file
unresolved_questions: Chrome.glideSpring's exact spring parameters, and therefore settlingDuration and the real flight duration, are defined outside this bundle
Numeric values of Chrome.rowCornerRadius, Chrome.inlineIconFont, Chrome.success and the Chrome.overlay(_:) mapping are outside this bundle
ObservedValue<Bool> is used but defined elsewhere; that it is an observable box is inferred from the comments only
Glide.hasLanded is written by land() but never read here, so whether another file reads it could not be established from the assigned files
The call sites of launch() and land(), presumably SidebarThreadRow or the sidebar list, and where RowGlideLayer is mounted in the window, are outside this bundle
hidingCells is never pruned, and whether that is an intentional bounded cache or a leak over long sessions cannot be judged from this file alone

feature_notes: Both layouts share one list, so a thread keeps its row when the layout changes and the row grows, shrinks and slides instead of being replaced; a settled thread however takes a different item id ("settled-<uuid>" vs the plain uuid string), so its open row leaves and a settled row arrives, and a reopen's ghost glides between the two

The sidebar doubles as a popover from the chat's Threads button (inPopover = true): no traffic-light clearance, no WindowDragArea, top padding 12 instead of 14, listFrame passed as nil so no glide can cross windows, and picking a thread calls dismiss()

The delete flow is deliberately ordered: the popover binding compares UUIDs only, confirmDeletion stores a ConfirmedDeletion and clears pendingDeletionID and pendingArchiveID, and carryOutConfirmedDeletion runs the delete in a Task only after the popover content's onDisappear; the comment records that the earlier ordering crashed in the presentation binding's getter after the row (and, in the Threads popover, the whole list) had been torn down
confirmBeforeDeleting == false deletes straight from the menu with no popover at all

Reorder: 4 pt of movement grabs the row under the pointer at the grab (settled and helper rows report no frame, so a drag from one goes nowhere); the grabbed row lifts with .scaleEffect(1.02), a Chrome.overlay(0.12) fill and .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.28), radius: 10, y: 4) on spring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.8); its own follow uses a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true; neighbours slide on spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.82); each swap fires .alignment haptics and re-takes DragPeers; release animates back on spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8). Fallback slot height for the crossing math is Chrome.rowHeight + 1

Slot height per peer = its measured row height + 1, plus, when unfolded, every non-head helper's height + 1 (default 24), plus, when heads show, one head-card height + 1 sized for (headCount + 5) / 6 rows; a folded parent adds the stub row's height + 1 instead
Helpers, the head card and the folded stub ride with a dragged parent through RidesWithDraggedParent (same offset, same zIndex 1), so a thread and everything under it travel as one block
Reordering is disabled while the search field has text

Scroll freeze: any scroll phase change or contentOffset.y change sets isListScrolling, which turns .allowsHitTesting off for the whole list so rows take no hover and no clicks; a 150 ms debounce task clears it, and an .idle phase cancels the task and clears it immediately; the flag is only written when it is false, to avoid one body pass per frame

Project layout order per project: pinned open threads, then the other open threads, then a 4 pt gap, then the Settled header, then the settled threads; settledCollapsed breaks out of the loop so nothing under the header is built at all. Projects are separated by a Chrome.groupGap spacer item and a folded project shows a count of its threads plus their helpers

Activity layout order: "Needs attention" (threads with approvals or questions, never settled) first, then "Pinned" open threads, then day groups of the rest by updatedAt, then the settled section sorted by AppModel.settledFirst; a helper whose parent is not shown stands on its own as a top-level row
needsAttention(thread) is true when model.existingRuntime(for:) has any approvals or any questions

placed(): newest updatedAt first, except threads with an activityOrder whose activityOrderDay is the same calendar day as updatedAt, which keep their dragged place in ascending order; a thread that became active after a reorder has no place and sorts to the top
Day titles: "Today", "Yesterday", the wide weekday name when fewer than 7 days old, month+day within the same year, otherwise month+day+year
orderedHeads: running heads first, newest createdAt first within each of running and finished
hydraAutoHidesIdleHeads hides the whole head card when no head is running; both the flag and the set of parents that still draw a card are part of the list cache key
The folded stub calls the group "heads" only when every folded thread is a Hydra head; any mix says "helpers"

Search matches a lowercased query against a per-thread lowercased title table (only changed titles are lowercased again), or against the project name, which then returns all of that project's threads and their helpers; each result carries the project's full thread count for its header row, and project rows in search results pass togglesExpansion: false

selected(for:) returns the session whose id matches selection[threadID], falling back to the LAST session in the thread, so a stale selection still shows a tab
open(...) appends the new session to the thread's array and immediately makes it the selection, returning it (@discardableResult)
run(_ script:threadID:directory:) is open(...) with script.name as the title and script.command as the startup command
ensureTerminal(threadID:directory:) opens a shell only when the thread has none

restart(_:) terminates the old shell and substitutes a fresh session at the same index in the row, keeping the title and directory and dropping any startup command (command: nil), then selects the fresh one; if the old session is no longer in the array the fresh one is appended
close(_:) terminates and removes the session, and if it was the selected one the selection falls back to the last remaining session's id, or nil when none remain
closeAll(for:) terminates every session of the thread and sets both sessions[threadID] and selection[threadID] to nil
terminateAll() terminates every session across every thread without clearing the dictionaries, an app-shutdown sweep
terminate() is idempotent: it returns early unless isRunning is true

foregroundJobIsTheShell returns false for a non-positive pid or a failed sysctl, and otherwise true only when the terminal foreground process group equals the shell's own process group

feature_notes: TourPage.id is a fresh UUID per init, so two TourPage values with identical text are still distinct for Identifiable and Hashable purposes.

The card's height is supplied by the caller (the window controller pre-measures the tallest page) so the card never grows or shrinks between pages; height: nil sizes to the current page and the comment says that is for previews and the empty state.
frame(width:height:) is applied twice: once on the non-empty branch's VStack and once on the enclosing Group, so the empty state also picks up the caller's frame.
advance(): on the last page it calls onFinish, else onClose, else the SwiftUI dismiss; otherwise it does currentIndex += 1. There is no wrap-around from the last page to the first.

goBack(): newIndex = max(0, currentIndex - 1) with an early return when unchanged, so pressing back on page 0 is a no-op; the back button is hidden by .opacity(0) on page 0 but is not disabled or removed, so its 32x32 hit area is still clickable there (a harmless no-op).
The close control (checkmark) calls onClose when provided, otherwise dismiss(); it never calls onFinish. In the shipped wiring both closures set hasSeenTour, so closing early still counts as seen.
clamped(_:pageCount:) returns 0 when pageCount is 0, else max(0, min(index, pageCount - 1)); it guards only the initial index, not later mutation.

artwork(for:) probes NSImage(named: page.imageName) first and only then draws Image(page.imageName).resizable().scaledToFill(); otherwise it draws the purple-to-near-black gradient placeholder with a photo glyph, so a missing asset degrades visibly instead of crashing. All eight referenced assets exist as tour-*.imageset in the catalog at this commit, so the placeholder branch is a safety net, not a shipped visual.

Both the image and the bottom panel carry .id(currentIndex) with .transition(.opacity), and the enclosing .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25), value: currentIndex) drives the 0.25s crossfade between pages.
Return/Enter activates the primary button via keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction); this file defines no arrow-key paging and no Escape handling.
The gradient seat is deliberately only 96pt tall and bottom-anchored: the comment says it is a seat for the page indicator only, so the scrim never reaches into the picture.

Header comment records provenance: a port of TourKit by Ram Patra (https://github.com/rampatra/TourKit, MIT License), the slideshow card, its page indicator and its controls, credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

feature_notes: present() is idempotent: when a window already exists it only calls makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil), activates the app and returns that same NSWindow, so a second call's pages and callbacks are ignored.

Height is measured once before the window appears: for each page it builds a TourBottomPanelSizingView with the finish title on the last page and the continue title otherwise, frames it to the width, hosts it in an NSHostingView, calls layoutSubtreeIfNeeded() and takes fittingSize.height, then takes .max() across pages (?? 0).
maxBottomPanelHeight returns 0 early for an empty page list, and the empty case then sizes the whole window to TourView.emptyStateHeight = 220.

The comment explains the fix this encodes: left to its defaults the hosting view resized the window to each page's own ideal height, so the card grew and shrank with the length of the description as the user paged.
The window is borderless with no titlebar controls: dismissal is only through TourView's checkmark, the Done button, or TourWindowController.close().

The onFinish closure handed to TourView falls back to the caller's onClose when onFinish is nil and always calls dismiss() (self.close()) afterwards; the onClose closure calls the caller's onClose then dismiss(). Tour.present supplies both, so either path persists hasSeenTour and then closes the window.
The dismiss closure captures self weakly, as does the WindowDelegate callback, which nils out both window and windowDelegate.
isReleasedWhenClosed = false together with windowWillClose clearing the references is what lets a later present() build a fresh window rather than resurrect a dead one.
isMovableByWindowBackground = true means the user drags the glass card itself to move the borderless window anywhere on screen.
collectionBehavior [.managed, .participatesInCycle, .fullScreenAuxiliary] keeps the card in window cycling and lets it appear over a full-screen space.

TourBottomPanelSizingView is private and used only for measurement: it renders a plain Text where the live view renders a Button, so the measured height assumes the glassProminent button occupies exactly the 220x42 frame.

purpose: Implements DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow by overriding AppKit's four private per-cycle 'window needs another pass' entry points and wrapping each super call in an @try/@catch that re-posts once on the next main-queue turn, logging both the first catch and a second consecutive catch to os_log.

Schedules a block on the main queue via dispatch_async to retry the pass request on the next run loop turn
Swallows NSException raised by AppKit inside the four private post methods

purpose: Holds the two verbatim system-prompt blocks the app injects for its anti-slop writing and editing guidance: the full enabled block headed '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance]' and the short cancellation block headed '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance: off]' used when the toggle is off.

Paragraph 1 verbatim: 'Give the shortest complete answer, leading with the result. Use plain, natural language. Skip filler, hype, stock openings, repeated summaries and unsolicited closers. Preserve requested detail, facts, uncertainty, blockers and required validation.'

Paragraph 2 verbatim: 'Make focused edits using existing patterns. Add comments only for non-obvious reasons, constraints or pitfalls; omit banners, obvious narration and speculative TODOs. Preserve useful documentation. Avoid unrelated cleanup, dependencies and abstractions.'

Paragraph 3 verbatim, containing a typographic right single quote in 'product’s': 'For UI work, follow the product’s components, typography and colors. Prefer purposeful structure and real content; preserve accessibility, responsive layouts and visible loading, empty and error states.'

Paragraph 4 verbatim: 'Reuse evidence, read relevant sections and batch independent lookups. Avoid repeated scans, polling and echoed logs. Perform required checks; brevity never excuses incomplete work. Apply this guidance to delegated work too. Report changes, affected files and material limits once. User requests and project requirements take precedence.'
disabledInstructions verbatim: header '[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance: off]' then 'Disregard earlier app-provided anti-slop guidance. Continue following user requests and project requirements.'

instructions(enabled:) is a single ternary returning enabledInstructions or disabledInstructions; there is no empty or nil case, so an off toggle still injects text. The comment above disabledInstructions explains why: 'Resumed conversations may still contain the enabled guidance.'
The product name 'Droppy Code' is hard-coded inside both prompt headers, so a rename changes the prompt text the model sees.

purpose: Incremental parsing of a lead's ```hydra delegation block while the reply is still streaming, so each head is dispatched the moment its JSON entry's outermost brace closes. Provides a stateless whole-text/whole-body reader (HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations), the shared single-entry reader HydraPrompts.delegation(fromEntry:) that the non-streaming parser in Hydra.swift also uses, and a stateful byte-at-a-time HydraDelegationStreamParser class that ingests only newly appended text.

feature_notes: streamedDelegations(in:) recognises only ```hydra and ```hydra-sent info strings (not ```hydra-leaving, unlike delegationOpener in Hydra.swift which also accepts -leaving)

streamedDelegations(inBody:) skips leading JSON whitespace (space, \n, \r, \t), then requires '[' (array, cursor advances past it) or '{' (one bare entry, cursor stays); any other first byte returns an empty, incomplete result

Termination conditions that set isComplete: ']' at depth 0, a '`' that opens a line at depth 0 (the closing fence), a '}' driving depth below 0 (broken block), or the closing '}' of a bare single entry

Each entry is parsed with JSONValue.parse on the substring from its opening brace to its closing brace inclusive; an entry that does not parse or that delegation(fromEntry:) rejects is silently skipped, so the streaming and whole-block parsers agree on order and count
atLineStart starts true because the body begins right after the opening fence's newline, and is updated as `byte == \n` after each byte
HydraDelegationStreamParser.ingest ignores further text once isComplete and breaks out of the byte loop as soon as isComplete flips

readOpener is a hand-written 16-state ASCII machine: states 0...2 count backticks (96), state 3 skips space (32) and tab (9) and extra backticks and requires 'h' (lowercased 104), states 4...7 require 'y' (121), 'd' (100), 'r' (114), 'a' (97), state 8 accepts '-' (45) to enter states 9...12 requiring 's' (115), 'e' (101), 'n' (110), 't' (116); states 13/14 accept trailing space/tab, '\r' (13) moves to state 15, '\n' (10) enters the body; a stray backtick anywhere resets the cursor to 1 rather than 0
The streaming class therefore accepts only ```hydra and ```hydra-sent, matching streamedDelegations(in:) and not the -leaving variant

readBody mirrors the stateless walk with raw ASCII codes: 34 '"', 92 '\\', 91 '[', 93 ']', 96 '`', 123 '{', 125 '}'; the entry accumulator is appended to only while depth > 0 and reset to [byte] on the outermost '{'
The class doc states it reads only newly appended UTF-8 bytes; completed or replaced messages get a fresh parser, and the runtime's sent watermark prevents already dispatched entries repeating

delegation(fromEntry:) drops an entry with a missing, non-string or whitespace-only "prompt"; an empty "task" is replaced by the 60-character single-line prompt title; empty-string name/project/profile are normalised to nil
The "name" an entry carries is passed through as-is for the spawner to resolve against the roster; an unknown "profile" falls back to the pair's shared worker model

TextCleanup.singleLine's exact truncation behaviour at limit 60 (ellipsis, word boundary) is defined in Core/Support/Text.swift, not read here

Project decode: id (required UUID), path (required String), name (default URL(fileURLWithPath: path).lastPathComponent), addedAt (default .now), isExpanded (default true), scripts (default []), hydraPairID (default nil), icon (default nil).
ProjectScript decode: id (default UUID()), name (required), command (required), symbol (default "play"), runOnWorktreeCreate (default false).

ChatThread decode defaults: title "New thread", createdAt .now, updatedAt = createdAt, provider .codex, model nil, effort nil, fastMode false, runtimeMode .supervised, interactionMode .build, worktreePath nil, branch nil, providerSessionID nil, providerResumeAt nil, isPinned false, isArchived false, isSettled false, settledAt nil, hasUnread false, hasCustomTitle false, sortOrder nil, activityOrder nil, activityOrderDay nil, lastStatus nil, parentThreadID nil, isInPanel false, expandsHelpers false, hydraEnabledIsExplicit false, hydraEnabled true, hydraPairID nil, hydraSpawnCount 0, hydra nil. id and projectID are required.
UserDefaults key "hydraDefaultEnabled" (Bool; absent means true), exposed as ChatThread.hydraDefaultKey
ui_elements: ChatThread.untitled = "New thread" is the placeholder title for a fresh chat.
Project.icon nil draws the folder mark in the activity list so a project reads at a glance before a mark is picked.
ProjectScript.symbol default "play" is the SF Symbol on the script button.
isSettled threads sit at the bottom of their sidebar list as a small grey row until reopened by hand or by a new turn; settledAt orders the latest settled first.

expandsHelpers off means helpers are folded behind one line under the chat that names the team, and a click unfolds them; it is saved under its own key so chats from before the fold was the default also fold.
isInPanel threads are kept out of the sidebar, the palette, the recent picks and the unread count while showing in the parent's floating panel.
feature_notes: Security-relevant decode: runtimeMode falls back to .supervised, with the comment that 'value' swallows a type mismatch as well as a missing key, so a thread must never quietly come back from disk with full access to the machine.

Hydra per-chat switch migration: a thread saved before the per-chat switch carried an ignored false under the same key and no hydraEnabledIsExplicit, so it decodes as hydraEnabled = true; after decode hydraEnabledIsExplicit is forced to true so every later save records a real user choice.
foldsHelpers is the inverted computed mirror of expandsHelpers: get { !expandsHelpers }, set { expandsHelpers = !newValue }.

ChatThread's memberwise init signature is (projectID:provider:model:effort:runtimeMode:fastMode:) with fastMode defaulting to false; it sets title to untitled, interactionMode .build, isPinned/isArchived/hasUnread/hasCustomTitle false, and hydraEnabled from hydraDefaultEnabled().
Project's memberwise init takes only (name:path:) and fills id = UUID(), addedAt = .now, isExpanded = true, scripts = [].
ProjectScript's memberwise init is (name:command:symbol:runOnWorktreeCreate:) with symbol defaulting to "play" and runOnWorktreeCreate to false.
Library.init(from:) decodes projects and threads as [Lenient<Project>] and [Lenient<ChatThread>] then compactMap(\.value), so one corrupt record does not lose the whole library.

Project.hydraPairID is the rule new chats in that project start on; nil means no rule and the app's remembered pair is used (comment names AppModel.newThread). The pair must be in Settings with its provider switched on or the rule does not apply.
ChatThread.hydraPairID is explicitly legacy: kept for decoding only, since new threads use the best fit for their provider and model.
hydraSpawnCount records how many heads this chat has sent out so far and gives the next head its place in the roster.

parentThreadID makes a thread a helper (a merge helper, for now); a helper opens in its parent's floating panel and afterwards sits under its parent in the sidebar as a smaller row for as long as the parent is there.

sortOrder is the thread's place after its project is reordered by dragging (nil keeps newest first); activityOrder plus activityOrderDay do the same inside the activity layout, and a thread active on a later day goes back to newest first.
unresolved_questions: HydraHeadInfo is declared in another file, so what a head record carries is not visible here.
CaptureRun.defaults is declared elsewhere; its nil behaviour is only inferable from the '?? .standard' fallback.
Lenient<T> and the value(_:default:) container helper live outside this bundle, so exactly which decoding errors they swallow is known only from this file's comments.

purpose: Defines the whole MCP domain model for Droppy Code: the three transports (stdio/http/oauth), the MCPField input descriptor, the MCPCategory taxonomy, the MCPCatalogEntry shape with its {key} placeholder fill/resolve logic, the resolved-server struct handed to providers and the probe, the persisted MCPConnection record, the probe result and tool summary, the setup-guide and connection-state enums, the MCPPaths file locations for the per-provider config files, and a Color(rgb:) initializer for the 0xRRGGBB brand tints.
key_symbols: enum MCPTransport (Sendable, Hashable): case stdio(command: String, args: [String]), case http(url: String, headers: [String: String]), case oauth(url: String)
struct MCPField (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): key, label, placeholder, kind (default .secret), help: String? = nil, defaultValue: String? = nil, isRequired = true; id { key }
enum MCPField.Kind: case secret, text, path

enum MCPCategory: String, CaseIterable, Sendable, Identifiable - developer, browser, search, work, data, cloud, knowledge; id { rawValue }; title switch returning "Developer", "Browser", "Search", "Work", "Data", "Cloud", "Knowledge"

struct MCPCatalogEntry (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): id, name, vendor, summary, category, asset, colorValue: UInt32, isMonochrome = false, transport, fields: [MCPField] = [], env: [String: String] = [:], docsURL, sampleTools: [String] = [], keysURL: String? = nil

struct MCPResolvedServer (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): id, name, command: String?, args: [String] = [], env: [String: String] = [:], url: String?, headers: [String: String] = [:], oauthUpstream: String?; isRemote { url != nil }
extension MCPCatalogEntry.fill(_ text: String, values: [String: String]) -> String
struct MCPToolSummary (Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): name, summary: String?; id { name }
struct MCPProbeResult (Sendable, Hashable): serverName: String?, serverVersion: String?, tools: [MCPToolSummary]

struct MCPConnection (Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): catalogID, isEnabled = true, values: [String: String] = [:], connectedAt: Date?, serverVersion: String?, tools: [MCPToolSummary] = []; id { catalogID }
struct MCPSetupGuide (Sendable, Hashable): title, reason, steps: [String], pageLabel, pageURL, note: String?
enum MCPConnectionState (Sendable, Hashable): notConnected, connecting, connected(toolCount: Int), failed(message: String), needsSetup(MCPSetupGuide); isConnected, isConnecting
enum MCPPaths: static directory, connectionsURL, customsURL, claudeConfigURL, codexConfigURL, copilotConfigURL
calls_into: MCPProxy.url(for: id) - used inside resolve() to point an OAuth server's url at the app's local proxy route
Storage.root - base URL for the mcp/ directory, mcp.json and custom-mcp.json
MCPKeychain (named in doc comments as where secret field values live)
MCPKeyPanel (named in the keysURL doc comment as the panel that opens the key page)
MCPOAuth (named in the .oauth transport doc comment as the sign-in implementation)
state_owned: MCPPaths.directory - a lazily-initialized static let URL (Storage.root/mcp, created on first access)
MCPPaths.connectionsURL, customsURL, claudeConfigURL, codexConfigURL, copilotConfigURL - static let URLs
MCPConnection is the persisted per-server user state value type (isEnabled, values, connectedAt, serverVersion, tools)
No ObservableObject or @State here; every type is a value type (struct/enum), all Sendable + Hashable
side_effects: MCPPaths.directory's initializer calls FileManager.default.createDirectory(at:withIntermediateDirectories: true) with try? - it creates Storage.root/mcp on first touch and silently swallows failure
No network, process launch, timers or Keychain access happen in this file itself; it only names the files and the Keychain store that other code uses
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI is imported solely for Color; Color(rgb:) builds a Color from Double components divided by 255 with no explicit color space
Swift concurrency Sendable conformance throughout, plus implicit-return switch bodies (Swift 5.9+) in MCPCategory.title
Storage.root is an app-owned macOS support directory
The generated config files target macOS CLI agents: `claude --mcp-config`, Codex app-server `config` overrides, `copilot --additional-mcp-config`
OAuth servers depend on a local HTTP proxy (MCPProxy) running in-process on the Mac
persisted_fields: Storage.root/mcp.json - JSON for [MCPConnection]; keys: catalogID (String), isEnabled (Bool, default true), values ([String:String], default empty), connectedAt (Date?), serverVersion (String?), tools ([MCPToolSummary], default empty)
MCPToolSummary persisted keys: name (String), summary (String?)
Storage.root/custom-mcp.json - JSON for [MCPCustomServer] (secret values never land here)
Storage.root/mcp/claude.json - {"mcpServers": {...}} for `claude --mcp-config`
Storage.root/mcp/codex.json - {"mcp_servers": {...}} for Codex's app-server config overrides
Storage.root/mcp/copilot.json - {"mcpServers": {...}} for `copilot --additional-mcp-config`
Secret field values are explicitly NOT stored in mcp.json; they live in the Keychain via MCPKeychain
ui_elements: MCPCategory.title strings used as section headings: "Developer", "Browser", "Search", "Work", "Data", "Cloud", "Knowledge"
MCPCatalogEntry.summary is documented as one line shown under the name on its card
MCPCatalogEntry.sampleTools is documented as three or four tools shown as the card's fine print
MCPCatalogEntry.asset names an Assets.xcassets image set of the form `mcp-<id>`, a template SVG tinted with `color`
isMonochrome = true means the brand mark is black or white and wears the text colour instead of colorValue

MCPSetupGuide drives a floating panel offered by the card: title (doc example "Turn on GitLab's MCP server"), reason, ordered steps, pageLabel (doc example "Open my groups"), pageURL, and an optional note shown under the buttons after a check that still fails
MCPConnectionState drives the page and composer display, including connected(toolCount:) and failed(message:)
feature_notes: Tool-call naming: the entry id is the server key in every provider config and therefore the server part of a tool call name, documented with the example `mcp__github__list_issues`; ids must be lowercase with hyphens only
fill() placeholder substitution: every `{key}` in text is replaced by values[key] (an empty string is treated as absent) else field.defaultValue else the empty string

Host-coercion rule in fill(): when a placeholder sits immediately after "://" (the test is `out.contains("://" + token)`), the value is trimmed of whitespace and newlines, a leading "https://" or "http://" is dropped (case-insensitive prefix test on the lowercased value), and all trailing "/" are removed - so pasting `https://gitlab.example.com/` yields `gitlab.example.com`

resolve() for .stdio: sets command, maps args through fill, and sets env = env.mapValues(fill).filter { !$0.value.isEmpty } so an optional field left empty drops its variable rather than passing an empty string
resolve() for .http: url = fill(url) and headers = headers.mapValues(fill) with empty values dropped the same way

resolve() for .oauth: server.url = MCPProxy.url(for: id) and server.oauthUpstream = fill(url) - the provider config never sees the real remote address, and no token ever sits in a config file because the proxy adds a fresh token per request
needsInput is true only when at least one field has isRequired == true, so an optional key (one that merely raises a rate limit) does not make a server need input
MCPConnectionState.isConnecting is implemented as `self == .connecting`, relying on the enum's synthesized Equatable
Color(rgb:) decodes 0xRRGGBB as red = (hex >> 16) & 0xFF / 255, green = (hex >> 8) & 0xFF / 255, blue = hex & 0xFF / 255
unresolved_questions: The `extension MCPCatalogEntry` block opens with a doc comment ("The launchable form, with `{key}` placeholders replaced by the user's values (or the field's default). OAuth servers resolve to their route on the app's proxy.") separated by a blank line from oauthURL's own doc comment, so it documents nothing; it reads like resolve()'s documentation stranded by a reordering, but intent cannot be confirmed from this file.
MCPProxy.url(for:) route shape, MCPOAuth's token flow, MCPKeychain's key naming and Storage.root's concrete path are all defined outside this bundle.
Whether Color(rgb:) yields sRGB or SwiftUI's default color space is not stated; Color(red:green:blue:) is called without a color space argument.

purpose: The hard-coded catalog of the 33 MCP servers Droppy Code ships with: each entry's id, display name, vendor, one-line summary, category, asset name, brand colour, transport (exact command and args, or exact remote URL and headers), credential fields with placeholder and help text, environment variables, docs URL, sample tool names and key-creation page. It also provides lookup by id, tolerant lookup by server name, a grouped-by-category view and the flat id list.
