feature_notes: start(): throws ProviderError.notInstalled(configuration.provider) when configuration.executable is nil; on resume it sends thread/resume with threadId plus excludeTurns=true and requires the returned thread.id to equal the requested id; otherwise thread/start. activeModel is taken from result["model"]. A defer closes and nils the connection when `started` never became true.

requestThread MCP retry: when the RPCError message contains "failed to load configuration" or "invalid transport" AND params.config.mcp_servers exists, it strips mcp_servers (and drops config entirely if that leaves it empty), retries the same method, and emits the MCP warning notice.

send(): content is input.command?.codexInput(for: input.text) or [["type":"text","text": text]]; each image where isImage appends {"type":"localImage","path": path}. It always sets "summary": "auto". An empty effort string is dropped. serviceTierForTurn comes from input.serviceTier. collaborationMode is sent only when a model resolves (input.model ?? activeModel), with mode "plan" for .plan interaction mode else "default", and settings {model, reasoning_effort (optional), developer_instructions: null}. The returned turn.id is stored in turnID.
interrupt() sends turn/interrupt with threadId and turnId, ignoring failures; compact() sends thread/compact/start with just threadId.

rollback(from:): a 30-second watchdog closes the connection. It pages thread/turns/list with limit 100, sortDirection "desc", itemsView "notLoaded", counting turns until targetID is found, then taking the next turn as previousID. It throws if nextCursor repeats the current cursor. Then thread/rollback with numTurns = count; the result must keep the same thread id, must no longer contain targetID, and its last remaining turn id must equal previousID. It clears turnID and returns threadID.
Rollback fallback: an RPCError containing "paginated threads do not support thread/rollback" routes to forkHistory.

forkHistory: with no previousID it archives the original thread, clears threadID and turnID, and returns nil. Otherwise it forks using threadParameters plus threadId, lastTurnId=previousID, excludeTurns=true; requires the new id to differ from the original; confirms via a 1-turn desc listing that the newest turn is previousID and not targetID; archives the original. On any failure it archives the NEW thread and rethrows. On success threadID becomes the new id, turnID is cleared, activeModel is refreshed.
threadParameters always sends cwd, approvalPolicy, sandbox, approvalsReviewer; model only when configuration.model is set.

Hydra native (hydra.runsNatively): merges HydraPrompts.codexConfig(hydra) into config with hydra's values winning on collision, and sets developerInstructions to HydraPrompts.policy(for: .codex, hydra).

Hydra non-native (heads on another provider, Droppy-run): sets config.features.multi_agent = false to switch off Codex's own agents whatever the user's config enables, and developerInstructions to HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy(hydra). The in-source comment records that words alone were not enough: a lead still reached for spawn_agent, ran its heads on itself, and the pair's model never saw them.

Anti-slop guidance rides along on every thread, Hydra or not: any existing developerInstructions and AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled: configuration.antiSlopEnabled) are joined with "\n\n" (nils compacted out), so the off notice still goes out and a resumed thread cannot keep earlier guidance alive.
MCPProviderConfig.codexOverrides() is merged into config["mcp_servers"] on top of whatever config already exists, never replacing it.

resolveApproval: .decision responds {"decision": payloads[optionID] ?? "cancel"}; .permissions responds {"permissions": requested, "scope": optionID} for optionID "turn" or "session" and {"permissions": {}, "scope": "turn"} otherwise; .question responds {"answers": {}}. It always emits .requestResolved(id:).
answerQuestion builds {"answers": {questionID: {"answers": [values]}}} and emits .requestResolved(id:).
stop() sets isStopping then closes the connection; handleClose resolves every pending request first and, unless stopping, emits .exited(error: TextCleanup.lastLines(tail)).
stopAgent(id) returns false unless the id is a known head with a live turn; it sends turn/interrupt on the head's own thread id.
listCommands: connects with no handlers, sets a 20-second watchdog, closes on defer, sends skills/list with cwds=[directory.path] and forceReload=true, and maps through SlashCommand.codexSkills.

listModels: connects against FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory, pages model/list at most 10 times following nextCursor, skips any model where hidden == true, requires an id, and falls back name -> id, isDefault -> false.
fastTier: builds "<id> <name>" lowercased and returns the first tier id whose label contains "fast" or "priority".

readPlanLimits: on a request failure it returns PlanLimits(planName: nil, windows: [], problem: plainProblem(error)). Snapshots come from rateLimitsByLimitId sorted by key, else the single non-null rateLimits object. Each snapshot's "primary" and "secondary" windows need a usedPercent double; window ids are "<limitId or 'codex'>-<key>"; resetsAt is treated as epoch seconds. With no windows it returns problem "Codex reported no usage windows for this account." with the parsed plan name.

plainProblem: TextCleanup.singleLine(String(describing: error), limit: 300); text containing "token_expired" or "401" becomes the codex login message; empty text becomes "Codex could not be asked for its usage."
parseResetCredits: requires availableCount or available_count; keeps credits with a non-empty id whose status is nil, "available" or "unknown"; availableCount is clamped with max(0, count).

resetDate accepts a number or numeric string (must be > 0), treating any value above 10_000_000_000 as milliseconds (divided by 1_000), else tries ISO 8601 with fractional seconds and then plain ISO 8601.

consumeResetCredit always sends idempotencyKey = UUID().uuidString.lowercased() and optionally creditId; it throws ResetCreditError.unknownOutcome when result.outcome is missing or not a PlanLimits.ResetOutcome raw value.

connect(): StdioProcess with arguments ["app-server"], JSONRPCConnection(process:, sendsVersion: false), a 20-second watchdog, an initialize request with clientInfo {name: "droppy-code", title: "Droppy Code", version: AppInfo.version} and capabilities {experimentalApi: true}; on failure it closes and rethrows; on success it sends the `initialized` notification.

handleNotification routes by params.threadId: a missing or matching id is the lead; a known head thread becomes .head(id) whose events are wrapped in .agentEvent(agentID:); notifications from any other thread on the same server are dropped entirely.
thread/started is handled before routing, by headStarted.
turn/started stores the turn id on the lead (turnID) or on headTurns[head], and emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID:).

item/agentMessage/delta -> .messageDelta; item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta and item/reasoning/textDelta -> .reasoningDelta; item/commandExecution/outputDelta -> .toolOutput; item/plan/delta -> .planDelta.
item/reasoning/summaryPartAdded emits a literal "\n\n" reasoning delta only when summaryIndex > 0.
turn/plan/updated maps step status "completed" -> .done, "inProgress" -> .active, anything else -> .pending, and emits .todos.
turn/diff/updated emits .diff(diff) when a diff string is present.

Lead token accounting on thread/tokenUsage/updated: emits ContextUsage(usedTokens: last.totalTokens ?? 0, windowTokens: tokenUsage.modelContextWindow). When total.totalTokens > 0 it calls spendTracker.spend(total:before: max(0, total - used)) so a resumed thread starts from total-minus-last rather than zero, and records only positive spend; otherwise it records `used` directly. The comment notes the thread total only ever grows within a session, so its positive deltas are exact spend however often the event fires.

Head token accounting mirrors the lead with a per-head TokenSpendTracker (a head's spend is the account's spend too) and additionally emits .agentProgress(agentID: head, summary: nil, lastTool: nil, tokens: total > 0 ? total : used, toolCalls: nil).
The "error" notification only raises a warning notice when it belongs to the lead and willRetry == true.

turn/completed maps turn.status "interrupted" -> .interrupted, "failed" -> .failed, default -> .completed; a null turn.error is treated as no error. For the lead it clears turnID, and a failed turn whose error matches UsageLimitSignal also emits .usageLimit(resetsAt: UsageLimitSignal.resetTime(in: error)) before .turnCompleted. For a head it clears headTurns[head] and emits .agentFinished(agentID:status:summary: error).
serverRequest/resolved clears a matching pending request by RPCID key and emits .requestResolved.

headStarted: a thread whose parentThreadId equals the lead's threadID is taken as a head. A thread naming another parent is still taken in when it carries agentNickname or agentRole (covering a resumed lead whose id rotated), and that case is logged at notice level with the thread id, the named parent (or "none") and this lead's id.

itemStarted: agentMessage emits a messageDelta of item.text (or ""), reasoning emits an empty reasoningDelta, plan emits a planDelta of item.text. A head's first userMessage becomes .agentStarted with the brief single-lined at 80 characters. hookPrompt, functionCallOutput and contextCompaction are ignored. Anything else that yields a ToolCall emits .toolStarted, and a collabAgentToolCall additionally registers its heads immediately so a completion lost to compaction never leaves them unknown.

itemCompleted: agentMessage -> .messageCompleted; reasoning joins summary[] with "\n\n" and falls back to content[] joined the same way; plan -> .planCompleted(markdown:). userMessage, hookPrompt, functionCallOutput and contextCompaction are ignored. Anything else that yields a ToolCall emits .toolStarted then .toolUpdated, and describeHeads runs on either target because the payload says whose head it is whatever thread the server filed it under.

describeHeads on collabAgentToolCall acts only when item.tool == "spawnAgent"; every receiverThreadIds entry is inserted into headThreads and announced as .agentStarted with toolUseID = item.id. A spawn whose item.model and item.reasoningEffort match exactly one HydraPrompts.nativeRoutableProfiles entry routes the head to that profile name; zero or several matches leave the head unrouted.

describeHeads on subAgentActivity registers an unseen agentThreadId as a head (logged at notice level explaining no thread/started or spawn receiver id preceded it, for older app-servers), then on kind "completed" or "interrupted" clears its turn and emits .agentFinished with the matching status and nil summary.

toolCall for commandExecution: when the set of commandAction types is exactly {"read"} and the first action has a path, it becomes a .read call titled by relative path with the unwrapped command as detail; when the set is non-empty and a subset of {"search", "listFiles"} it becomes .search titled by the command; otherwise .command. The command is always unwrapped via ToolTitles.unwrapShell.
toolCall for fileChange titles a single change by relative path, otherwise "Edit <n> files", kind .edit.
toolCall for mcpToolCall sets detail to the compact arguments string unless that string is literally "null".

toolCall for dynamicToolCall -> .other titled by item.tool; webSearch -> .web titled by item.query; imageView -> .read titled by relative path; imageGeneration -> .other titled by revisedPrompt; enteredReviewMode/exitedReviewMode -> .other titled "Review" with item.review as detail.
toolCall returns nil for subAgentActivity, so those rows draw nothing; the comment explains they only doubled the head's report pill as "Delegated Head finished".

toolUpdate for commandExecution sets output from aggregatedOutput and exitCode from exitCode; for fileChange it builds FileEdits with relative paths and ToolTitles.diffStats additions/deletions; for mcpToolCall it prefers error.message, else joins result.content[].text with "\n"; webSearch, imageView, enteredReviewMode and exitedReviewMode are marked .completed unconditionally.
toolStatus maps "inProgress" -> .running, "failed" and "interrupted" -> .failed, "declined" -> .declined, and otherwise .failed when a non-zero exitCode exists else .completed.
errorMessage takes error.message or error.displayText, and when that raw text itself parses as JSON containing error.message or message, the nested message wins.

decisionOptions defaults availableDecisions to ["accept", "acceptForSession", "decline", "cancel"]; an object decision carrying acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment adds the "amend" option only for command approvals; options are sorted into the order approve, approveAlways, decline, cancel (missing roles sort as index 0).

handleRequest covers item/commandExecution/requestApproval (title is the unwrapped command or "Command", detail is the relative cwd), item/fileChange/requestApproval, item/permissions/requestApproval, item/tool/requestUserInput, and mcpServer/elicitation/request which is auto-declined with {"action":"decline"} plus a warning notice; every other method gets JSON-RPC error -32601.
Question requests always set allowsMultiple: false; allowsOther comes from isOther and isSecret from isSecret (both default false); header and prompt fall back to empty strings; choices need a label.

policySettings mapping by RuntimeMode: .supervised -> approvalPolicy "untrusted", sandbox "read-only", sandboxPolicy {"type":"readOnly"}, reviewer "user"; .autoAcceptEdits -> "on-request", "workspace-write", {"type":"workspaceWrite"}, "user"; .auto -> "on-request", "workspace-write", {"type":"workspaceWrite"}, "auto_review"; .fullAccess -> "never", "danger-full-access", {"type":"dangerFullAccess"}, "user".

threadParameters sends the `sandbox` string form while send() sends the `sandboxPolicy` object form alongside approvalPolicy and approvalsReviewer on every turn, so the runtime mode can change between turns without restarting the thread.
unresolved_questions: The exact shape of HydraPrompts.codexConfig(hydra) (which Codex config keys it sets) is not visible here; only that its keys win over any already in `config` on merge.
MCPProviderConfig.codexOverrides() returns the JSONValue placed at config.mcp_servers, but its structure and the file it reads are defined elsewhere.
TurnInput.command.codexInput(for:) (how a slash command becomes input content parts) is defined outside this file.
JSONValue's .compactString and .displayText formatting rules are not defined here, so the exact MCP arguments detail text and the raw error text cannot be pinned from this file alone.
PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:) and PlanLimitsReader.codexPlanName(_:) produce the user-visible window and plan names; their literals live in another file.
Whether `sendsVersion: false` on JSONRPCConnection omits the jsonrpc version field or some client-version field is not determinable from this file.
UsageLimitSignal.matches/resetTime matching patterns are not in this file.
PlanLimits.ResetOutcome's raw values are not listed here, only that result.outcome must parse into one.

The file has no compile-time conditionals or feature flags and every branch appears reachable at runtime; the acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment option and the thread/rollback-to-fork fallback are version-dependent on the installed app-server, which this source alone cannot determine.

feature_notes: start(): connects, then uses configuration.resumeID ?? UUID().uuidString.lowercased() as sessionId and calls "session.create" when resumeID is nil, otherwise "session.resume"; a resume for an id the CLI no longer has fails so the thread starts fresh. After create/resume it always calls applyModes(runtime:interaction:) (a resumed session comes back interactive + manual) and loadCommands(), then returns the id.
Auto mode requires the CLI's experimental flag isExperimentalMode, which is a session-creation setting, so switching into or out of Auto forces the thread to restart the session.

systemMessage is always sent as {mode:"append"} exactly once per session; the content is [hydraPolicy, AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled:)] compactMap'd and joined with "\n\n", so the anti-slop OFF notice still goes out and a resumed thread cannot keep earlier guidance alive.

Hydra native mode sets customAgents = HydraPrompts.copilotAgents(hydra) and includeSubAgentStreamingEvents = true with policy HydraPrompts.policy(for: .copilot, hydra); Hydra heads on another provider instead use HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy(hydra) and define no CLI agents.

send(): applies modes and model/effort selection first, then beginTurn(); if the text starts with a slash command the CLI knows (commandNames), it calls session.commands.invoke, otherwise session.send. On a throw turnActive is reset to false before rethrowing.
beginTurn() clears shownReasoning and streamedMessages, resets turnError and interruptRequested, and emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID: nil).

Image attachments: only images (Attachment.isImage) are passed, as {"type":"file","path":...,"displayName":...,"mimeType":...} in an "attachments" array; the CLI reads the files itself for vision models.

invokeCommand(): reads result.mode to flip interactionMode ("plan" -> .plan, anything else -> .build) and emits .modeChanged; result.kind "agent-prompt" re-sends result.prompt (or the raw input) as a prompt; "text"/"completed" emits an ANSI-stripped message and finishes the turn; any other kind emits the warning notice and finishes the turn.

ownCommands are intercepted and never registered: allow-all, yolo, permissions, model, models, plan, session, sessions, cwd, cd. Aliases from the CLI list are added to commandNames but only the primary name produces a SlashCommand entry (name + description detail).
interrupt(): only acts while turnActive; sets interruptRequested, cancels every pending request, then session.abort with reason "user_initiated".
compact(): session.history.compact with trigger "manual".

rollback(turns:): lists session.history.listRewindPoints, requires points.count >= turns and takes points[count - turns].eventId, then session.history.rewind with mode "conversation"; failures throw "Copilot has no rewind point for that turn." or result.error / "Copilot could not rewind the conversation." (outcome must equal "success"). File state is not restored here; Droppy Code restores it from its own checkpoints.

resolveApproval(): "allow" -> {kind:"approve-once",approvedInteractively:true}; "always" -> sessionApproval(for:) or the same approve-once; anything else -> {kind:"reject",feedback:"The user declined this action."} and the tool row is marked .declined. Always emits .requestResolved(id:).
Declining a question through resolveApproval answers {answer:"", wasFreeform:true}; answerQuestion joins the first answers value with ", " and sets wasFreeform to !choices.contains(answer).

Plan approval answers {approved:true, selectedAction:"interactive"} and optimistically emits .modeChanged(.build); refusal answers {approved:false, feedback:"The user wants to keep planning. Wait for their feedback before changing anything."}.
stop(): sets isStopping so handleClose does not emit .exited, requests runtime.shutdown (to let the CLI flush its event log) then closes, with a 3 second timer closing as a backstop.

permissionModeName: .supervised and .autoAcceptEdits -> "manual", .auto -> "assisted", .fullAccess -> "allow-all"; session.permissions.setMode is sent with source "rpc" and the reply's mode is trusted (assisted is refused outside experimental mode).
session.mode.set uses "plan" or "interactive".

applySelection(): session.model.switchTo {modelId, reasoningEffort?} only when the model actually changed; a separate session.model.setReasoningEffort when only the effort changed. Local model/effort state is only updated when the request succeeded.

connect(): CLI arguments are exactly --headless --stdio --no-auto-update --log-level error plus MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments(); Settings-connected MCP servers are the only ones the session sees and the user's own are disabled by name for that session without touching their file. The handshake is a `ping` with {"message":"droppy-code"} and a non-nil protocolVersion, else the connection closes and it throws "This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`."

handleNotification only handles method "session.event"; events for a different sessionId are dropped. With Hydra off, sub-agent events (agentId present) whose type starts with "assistant." or "tool." are dropped except "assistant.usage", so spend still counts; permission prompts always pass. With Hydra on, agent events are wrapped in .agentEvent(agentID:_:).

Event types handled: assistant.turn_start, assistant.message_delta, assistant.message, assistant.reasoning_delta, assistant.reasoning, assistant.usage, session.usage_info, tool.execution_start, tool.execution_partial_result, tool.execution_progress, tool.execution_complete, subagent.started, subagent.completed, subagent.failed, permission.requested, permission.completed, session.mode_changed, session.title_changed, session.error, session.warning, session.compaction_complete, session.idle, session.shutdown. Everything else is ignored.
assistant.turn_start from a head emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID: data.turnId) on the head sink; for the lead it only sets turnActive and emits when a turn was not already active.

assistant.usage spend = inputTokens + outputTokens and is only reported when > 0; TokenSpend carries cachedInputTokens from cacheReadTokens, model from data.model ?? the session model, and agentID for head spend.
session.usage_info -> ContextUsage(usedTokens: currentTokens, windowTokens: tokenLimit).
tool.execution_partial_result maps partialOutput to .toolOutput; tool.execution_progress maps progressMessage to a ToolUpdate(detail:).

subagent.started (Hydra only) emits AgentSpawn with taskID nil, toolUseID = data.toolCallId, description = the stored task brief, else agentDisplayName, else agentName, else "Subagent"; profile via HydraPrompts.profileName(forAgentName: data.agentName). subagent.completed maps cancelled == true to .interrupted otherwise .completed with no summary; subagent.failed maps to .failed with data.error as summary.
session.idle ends the turn: finishTurn(aborted: data.aborted == true). A turn that was interrupted or aborted reports .interrupted, a recorded turnError reports .failed, otherwise .completed.
session.error while a turn is active is stashed in turnError and surfaced at turn end; outside a turn it becomes an .error Notice immediately.
session.mode_changed maps "plan" -> .plan and both "interactive" and "autopilot" -> .build; other values are ignored.
session.shutdown only notices when shutdownType == "error" and errorReason exists.
session.compaction_complete: success true -> info notice "Context compacted."; otherwise the error string becomes a warning notice.

Reasoning dedupe: reasoning shown by assistant.reasoning is hashed (trimmed hashValue) into shownReasoning so a message's own reasoningText copy is not repeated; the message-carried copy is emitted with id "<messageId>-reasoning".

assistant.message emits .messageCompleted even with empty content when that id previously streamed deltas, so an empty final message still closes the row; it then registers every entry of toolRequests as a tool row.

toolRequested is idempotent per call id (guard toolNames[id] == nil). "update_todo" is intercepted and turned into .todos from its markdown checklist instead of a row; "task" stores the brief (description ?? name ?? "Subagent", prompt ?? task) so subagent.started can name the head. A call with non-empty edits immediately gets a follow-up ToolUpdate(edits:).

handleToolResult skips hiddenTools; output prefers error.message on failure, otherwise result.detailedContent ?? result.content; status is .completed, or .declined when the id is in declinedTools, else .failed. success defaults to true when absent.

errorMessage(): default "Copilot reported an error."; text after the marker "GenericFailure, " is parsed as JSON and rewritten as "HTTP <status>: <trimmed body>"; when statusCode == 403, remediation == "sign_in", or the message contains "not authorized to use this Copilot feature" (case-insensitive) it appends " Check that your GitHub account has Copilot access, or sign in again with `copilot login`."

Server requests: userInput.request becomes a QuestionRequest keyed "question-<id.key>"; exitPlanMode.request becomes a plan approval keyed "plan-<id.key>" using planContent (non-empty) ?? summary ?? ""; autoModeSwitch.request is answered {"response":"no"} so a rate limit cannot silently move the user off their chosen model; any other method gets JSON-RPC error -32601 "Droppy Code does not support <method>."

handlePermission ignores requests with resolvedByHook == true. automaticDecision approves everything in .fullAccess, approves kind "write"/"read" in .autoAcceptEdits, approves write/read plus anything the CLI's assistedApproval recommendation == "approve" in .auto, and approves nothing in .supervised; the approve payload is {"kind":"approve-once"} with no approvedInteractively flag.
A "write" permission that carries a non-empty diff updates the tool row with the CLI's own patch (FileEdit with ToolTitles.diffStats additions/deletions) because it beats the row's reconstruction.
When the approval has no reason, promptRequest.assistedApproval.reason (the judge's words) is used instead.

sessionApproval(for:): shell needs canOfferSessionApproval == true and non-empty commands[].identifier -> {kind:"commands", commandIdentifiers:[...]}; write needs canOfferSessionApproval -> {kind:"write"}; read -> {kind:"read"}; url returns {kind:"approve-for-session", domain:<URL host>} directly; mcp -> {kind:"mcp", serverName, toolName(optional)}; custom-tool -> {kind:"custom-tool", toolName}; memory -> {kind:"memory"}; anything else nil. All but the url case are wrapped as {kind:"approve-for-session", approval: ...}.
respondPermission always posts session.permissions.handlePendingPermissionRequest with {sessionId, requestId, result}.

cancelPendingRequests answers permissions with {kind:"cancelled", reason:"The user stopped the turn."}, questions with JSON-RPC error -32800 "The user stopped the turn.", and plan exits with {approved:false, feedback:"The user stopped the turn."}, emitting .requestResolved for each.
handleClose resolves every pending request, clears turnActive, and (unless isStopping) emits .exited with TextCleanup.lastLines(tail).

Tool mapping: MCP calls (server present) become .mcp "<server> \u00b7 <tool>"; bash/powershell -> .command with the command text and the description as detail; read_bash/write_bash/stop_bash/list_bash -> .command humanized with shellId detail; view -> .read with a view_range detail; create/edit -> .edit with a FileEdit built from file_text or old_str/new_str; str_replace_editor dispatches on its command argument (view/create/insert/default); apply_patch parses the envelope's "*** Update File: ", "*** Add File: ", "*** Delete File: " headers into deduped paths; grep/glob -> .search with pattern and joined paths; web_fetch/web_search -> .web; task -> .agent with "<name> \u00b7 <agent_type>" detail; read_agent/write_agent/list_agents -> .agent; skill -> .other "Skill \u00b7 <skill>"; sql -> .other with the query as detail; create_pull_request -> .other; anything else -> .other humanized with a single-line compact-argument detail.
apply_patch reads the patch from the bare argument string, else arguments.input, else arguments.patch; the title is the single relative path when there is one, otherwise "Edit <count> files".

todos(from:) parses a markdown checklist where the marker may be -, *, + or "<digits>."/"<digits>)": "x" (case-insensitive) -> .done, " " or empty -> .pending, anything else inside the brackets -> .active.
humanize() replaces "-" and "_" with spaces and uppercases only the first character.

The header documents that Copilot offers no way to stop a single Hydra head on its own, and that the protocol was verified live against copilot 1.0.83 (protocol version 3): framing, ping, account auth, session create/resume/delete, commands, agent and permission modes, model and effort switching, rewind points, compaction and the event envelope.
unresolved_questions: MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments() is not in this file, so the exact flags it appends (and how user MCP servers are switched off by name) cannot be stated from here.
HydraPrompts.copilotAgents/policy/fallbackPolicy/profileName and AntiSlopPolicy.instructions are external, so the actual system-message and customAgents content is unknown from this file.
JSONRPCConnection's sendsVersion: true behavior (whether it adds a jsonrpc field or a protocol version field) is defined elsewhere; only the call site is visible here.
ProviderRegistry.copilotAuto's id/name/efforts, which is prepended ahead of every listed model, is defined outside this file.
PlanLimitsReader.planName(_:) mapping from the raw copilot_plan string to a display name is external.
The header mentions session delete was verified live, but no session.delete call exists in this file, so where a Copilot session is deleted is not determinable from here.
loadCommands() runs in a detached Task, so whether a slash command typed immediately after start() reliably finds commandNames populated is a race this file does not resolve.

A response that already streamed a Hydra head delegation (HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations(in: content)) is never retried; the error text appends "This response was not retried because it had already streamed a head delegation."
StreamCoalescer batches consecutive text or reasoning and flushes at most 30 ms (.milliseconds(30)) after the first piece; switching between text and reasoning forces an immediate flush
SSE drain: lines are trimmed, only lines with the "data:" prefix are used, "[DONE]" ends the stream, and json["error"] yields a stream error using error.message or displayText

Usage parsing accepts prompt_tokens or input_tokens, completion_tokens or output_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens or input_tokens_details.cached_tokens or prompt_cache_hit_tokens, and total_tokens falling back to input + output
Delta parsing reads choices[0].delta.content, delta.reasoning_content or delta.reasoning, and delta.tool_calls[].index/.id/.function.name/.function.arguments with index defaulting to 0
Non-200 responses read up to 8_000 characters of the body; errorMessage prefers error.message then message, else the first 500 characters of the trimmed body, else "<title> returned status <code>."
Six built-in tools with the exact names read_file, list_files, search_text, write_file, edit_file, run_command, plus MCP tools appended; tool_choice is "auto" and stream is true

read_file description states the whole file by default and start_line/line_count for large files; edit_file requires old_string to appear exactly once and also accepts legacy argument names old_text and new_text

readOnlyKind maps read_file to .read and list_files/search_text to .search; consecutive approval-free reads run concurrently with maxConcurrentReads = 4 while preserving the model order, and anything else acts as a barrier
requiresApproval: plan mode blocks .edit and .command even after "Approve for turn"; supervised asks for everything; autoAcceptEdits and auto ask only for .command; fullAccess asks for nothing
trimHistory keeps the system message plus at most 50 body messages once the count exceeds 60, and never cuts the running turn because it slices from the last user message
compact() keeps the system message plus the last 10 messages, only when messages.count > 12, then sanitizes
sanitizeHistory drops orphaned tool messages and strips tool_calls that lost their answers, deleting an assistant message that ends up with neither calls nor content
Output summary limits per tool: read_file 4_000, list_files 4_000, search_text 6_000, MCP 12_000, run_command 12_000 characters, each with "\n…(truncated)"

searchText runs /usr/bin/grep with ["-R", "-n", "-I", "--exclude-dir=.git", "--exclude-dir=node_modules", "--exclude-dir=.build", "--exclude-dir=build"], then -E or -F, then "--", pattern, target; timeout 30, outputLimit 64_000; results cap at 120 lines with "\n…(<n> matches, truncated)" and "(no matches)" when empty; the path goes through NativeFileTools.resolveURL so it cannot escape the project, fixing a noted past vulnerability that grepped ~/.ssh
runCommand runs /bin/zsh -lc with LoginEnvironment.current, timeout 120, outputLimit 24_000, and prefixes an over-24_000-byte output with "…" keeping the suffix

System prompt opens "You are Droppy Code’s <agentIdentity(model)>, working inside <workingDirectory> on macOS." with four mode-line variants (plan, build+supervised, build+autoAcceptEdits/auto, build+fullAccess), then six Rules bullets including "Never hard-wrap prose at a fixed column" and "Today’s date is <ISO8601 now>", then the Hydra policy, the AntiSlopPolicy instructions and the project guidance block
refreshSystemPrompt rewrites messages[0] at the start of each turn so edited AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md rules take effect on a resumed thread

Images: at most 4 attachments where isImage, only when config.isVisionModel(currentModel); otherwise the text gains "\n\n[Attached images (model cannot see them): <names>]"; images are sent as {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:<mime>;base64,<data>"}}
assistantTurn always sets role and content, adds reasoning_content only when config.replaysReasoning, and adds tool_calls entries of {id, type: "function", function: {name, arguments}}

start() reuses configuration.resumeID or a lowercased UUID, seeds the messages array with the system prompt plus the saved transcript mapped to user/assistant roles, and deliberately emits no .models event because the registry owns the live catalog

Hydra head pacing: budgetSpent when toolsUsed >= HydraBudget.maxTools or elapsed >= HydraBudget.maxSeconds, a one-time wrap-up note at wrapUpTools or wrapUpSeconds, and a pacing note every HydraBudget.pacingTools tools without a write_file or edit_file
The final-report round (input.isFinalReport or budget spent) is streamed with withTools: false
reportUsage emits .usage plus TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:) and a .tokenSpend event only when ReportedTokenUsage.hasSpend (total, input or output greater than zero)
nextID format is "<prefix>-<counter>-<first 8 characters of a UUID>" with prefixes "message", "thought", "tool", "approval", "plan"
In plan mode a non-empty final text emits .planCompleted(id: "plan-...", markdown: finalText) before .turnCompleted
answerQuestion(_:answers:) is an empty no-op: these providers never ask structured questions

purpose: Reads the subscription usage windows for whichever providers Pi is OAuth-signed into, by taking the access tokens Pi stores in <config>/auth.json and calling Anthropic's and ChatGPT's own usage endpoints, so Droppy Code's usage panel can show the same windows Pi's TUI shows without owning the logins itself.

side_effects: Reads <config>/auth.json from disk
Network: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with a 15 second timeoutInterval
Network: GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage with a 15 second timeoutInterval
Sends the user's OAuth bearer tokens to those two hosts

persisted_fields: <config>/auth.json entries, per provider key: type (String, must equal "oauth"), access (String access token, must be non-empty), expires (Double, milliseconds since epoch, compared as expires/1_000 against Date.now)
Recognized auth.json keys: "anthropic" -> Anthropic usage; "openai-codex" or "openai" -> Codex usage; all other keys are skipped
Anthropic response fields: limits (array, passed through to PlanLimitsReader.parseClaudeUsage), subscription_type (String -> plan name)

Codex response fields: rate_limit (object, falling back to the root), primary_window, secondary_window, used_percent (Double), limit_window_seconds (Int), reset_at (Double, epoch seconds), reset_after_seconds (Int), plan_type (String)
JWT claim path for the account id: ["https://api.openai.com/auth"]["chatgpt_account_id"] (String)
ui_elements: Anthropic plan name: "Claude " + PlanLimitsReader.planName(subscription_type), or plain "Claude" when absent
Anthropic window titlePrefix passed to parseClaudeUsage: "Claude"
Codex plan name: "Codex " + PlanLimitsReader.codexPlanName(plan_type), or plain "Codex"
Codex window title: "Codex · " + PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes: limit_window_seconds / 60) (middle dot with surrounding spaces)
Codex window ids: "codex-primary" and "codex-secondary"
Combined plan name when several providers report: the individual names joined with " · "
feature_notes: Providers are visited in sorted key order of the auth.json object, so combined plan names and window order are deterministic
An entry whose type is not "oauth", whose access token is empty, or whose expires (ms/1000) is already in the past is skipped without any network call
read returns nil when auth.json is missing/unparsable, when it is not an object, or when no provider produced a window
planName is nil when every contributing provider returned a nil planName
Anthropic request headers: Authorization "Bearer <token>", anthropic-beta "oauth-2025-04-20", Accept "application/json"; a non-200 status, a transport error or an unparsable body yields nil
Codex request headers: Authorization "Bearer <token>", Accept "application/json", plus ChatGPT-Account-Id taken from the JWT payload when the claim is present and non-empty
Codex reset time prefers reset_at (absolute epoch seconds) and falls back to Date.now + reset_after_seconds; when neither is present resetsAt is nil but the window is still produced

A model change mid-session sends {"type":"set_model","provider":...,"modelId":...} and then re-reads get_state purely to refresh contextWindow; an effort change sends {"type":"set_thinking_level","level":...}

Prompts are sent as {"type":"prompt","message":<text>} with an optional "images" array of {type:"image", data:<base64>, mimeType:<mime>} built only from attachments where isImage is true and the bytes load
interrupt() sends {"type":"abort"}; compact() sends {"type":"compact"} and throws ProviderError.notRunning when not running
stopAgent(_:) always returns false: Pi has no sub-agent stop support here
Streaming ids are namespaced per launch: messages "<launchID>-m-<n>", thinking "<launchID>-t-<n>", plans "<launchID>-plan-<turnCounter>"
message_start is ignored unless message.role == "assistant"; it bumps the message counter and clears messageText/thinkingText/currentThinkingID

handleUpdate reads assistantMessageEvent, falling back to event; text_delta accumulates into messageText and emits .messageDelta (creating a message id if none exists yet), thinking_delta accumulates into thinkingText and emits .reasoningDelta

The four fallbacks are split into named locals with a comment that the single summed expression makes `swiftc -typecheck` fail with "unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time"

message_end prefers the joined text of the message's content blocks of type "text" over the accumulated deltas when that join is non-empty; it emits .reasoningCompleted when thinkingText has non-whitespace, then .messageCompleted, and records lastReplyText; stopReason == "error" sets turnError from errorMessage or "Pi reported an error."
Tool kinds by name: bash -> .command, read -> .read, edit/write -> .edit, grep/find/ls -> .search, any name starting with "mcp__" -> .mcp, anything else -> .other

Tool titles: bash uses ToolTitles.unwrapShell(args.command); read/edit/write use ToolTitles.relativePath(args.path, to: workingDirectory); grep/find use args.pattern; ls uses args.path defaulting to "."; mcp__ names split on "__" into server (index 1) and tool (indices 2... rejoined with "__"); other tools use the raw name with the pretty-printed args as detail when they are not null and not "{}"
A `write` call snapshots the target file at tool_execution_start so the row's diff is before-vs-written; files larger than 1_000_000 bytes are not snapshotted (snapshot returns nil, stored as "")
tool_execution_update emits .toolOutput with the text extracted from partialResult.content (string, or the joined "text" fields of content blocks separated by "\n")

Tool status: completed unless isError (message.isError or result.isError); an error output beginning with "The user declined this" is reported as .declined rather than .failed; exitCode comes from result.details.exitCode

unifiedDiff is deliberately minimal: a --- / +++ header then every non-empty old line prefixed "-" followed by every non-empty new line prefixed "+"; `let relative = path.hasPrefix("/") ? path : path` is a no-op ternary that always yields the path unchanged
edit diffs use args.oldText vs args.newText; write diffs use the snapshot vs args.content (the snapshot is consumed with removeValue)

finishTurn is driven by agent_end (and by a failed prompt response); in plan mode with no error and no interrupt it first emits .planCompleted with the last reply as markdown, then emits .turnCompleted with .interrupted / .failed(error) / .completed
A response line whose id has no waiting continuation but whose command == "prompt" and success == false sets turnError from error or message and finishes the turn

extension_ui_request ids are read from id or requestId; methods handled: select, confirm, input, editor, notify; setStatus, setWidget, setTitle and set_editor_text are explicitly accepted and ignored (break), as is any unknown method
notify maps notifyType "warning" -> .warning, "error" -> .error, anything else -> .info

handleSelect recognizes the gate by the title prefix "droppy-gate " and parses the JSON that follows it; a session grant for the payload's kind answers "Allow" immediately without prompting; otherwise an ApprovalRequest is raised carrying the payload's toolCallId as toolItemID
Session grants are keyed by grantKey: .command -> "command", .fileChange -> "fileChange", .tool/.permissions/.plan -> "tool", which matches the kind strings the extension puts in the payload
answerQuestion sends {"cancelled": true} when no answer text was given, {"confirmed": <text == "Yes">} for confirm, and {"value": <first text>} otherwise, then emits .requestResolved

didClose reads the stderr tail through TextCleanup.lastLines, fails any active turn (interrupted when an interrupt was requested), and, unless stop() was called, emits .exited with nil for status 0 or "Pi exited with status <status>" plus the tail

Whether pi attaches any extra meaning to that string could not be determined from these files.

`let relative = path.hasPrefix("/") ? path : path` in unifiedDiff appears to be a leftover of an intended relative-path conversion; whether absolute paths in diff headers are intentional cannot be settled here.

handleSelect's non-gate fallback stores pendingQuestions[id] = "select", which answerQuestion handles through its generic `value` branch; whether pi expects a different field for a select response was not verifiable from this file.

The `permissions` and `plan` ApprovalRequest.Kind cases are never produced by this session (only .command/.fileChange/.tool are), so their grantKey mapping to "tool" is unreachable here; the cases are defined elsewhere.

A stored token expiring within the next 300 seconds triggers `claude auth status` and a re-read of the credentials before the request
On HTTP 401 or 403 the login is refreshed once and retried, and only if the re-read access token actually differs from the previous one

Keychain output starting with "{" is used as-is; otherwise an even-length all-hex string is hex-decoded to bytes before JSON parsing
ClaudeLogin.planName capitalizes subscriptionType and appends the first \d+x match from rateLimitTier in parentheses, e.g. "max" + "default_claude_max_20x" -> "Max (20x)"
Usage request headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, Accept: application/json, timeoutInterval 15

CLI fallback launches `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose` in the system temporary directory, sends request_id "droppy-code-init" with {"subtype":"initialize","hooks":null}, then on its response sends request_id "droppy-code-usage" with {"subtype":"get_usage"}
The CLI usage response is read from response.response.rate_limits (and its own "limits" array) with the plan name from response.response.subscription_type

The five_hour/seven_day fallback is only consulted when the limits array produced no windows at all; extra usage is appended regardless, but only when extra_usage.is_enabled is true
parseClaudeUsage returns nil when no windows were produced, so the caller falls through to the next source
parseDate strips any fractional-second group matching \.\d+ before ISO8601 parsing, because Claude writes microsecond timestamps the ISO 8601 parser rejects

PlanLimits.problem exists so an expired login can be shown in the provider's own words instead of stale bars; resetCredits is documented as Codex-only and may hold fewer credits than availableCount when only a total was reported

purpose: Builds the 'Project guidelines' system-prompt block for native API sessions (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai) by reading exactly AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the working directory root, caching the rendered block and re-rendering only when a file's size or modification date changed.

side_effects: Reads files from disk: <workingDirectory>/AGENTS.md and <workingDirectory>/CLAUDE.md
Stats those files (attributesOfItem) on every systemPromptBlock() call
Streams file bytes with FileHandle in chunks of min(65_536, perFileLimit + 1 - data.count)
No network, no process launch, no persistence

attributes[.type] compared against FileAttributeType.typeRegular to reject devices, sockets and directories
feature_notes: Injection order is fixed: AGENTS.md first, then CLAUDE.md (Self.fileNames order).
Per-file byte cap 16000; combined cap across all files 24000, tracked by a `remaining` counter decremented by each included file's byte count.

A file whose bytes exceed perFileLimit or the remaining budget is NOT dropped silently: the section text is exactly "\(name) is too large to include here (\(size) bytes). Read \(name) with the read_file tool; it may contain rules the project expects you to follow." where size is the on-disk size attribute, falling back to data.count.
A file that cannot be opened yields exactly "Could not load \(name). Read it with the read_file tool before changing the project."
A file that is not valid UTF-8, or whose text trims to empty under .whitespacesAndNewlines, is skipped entirely: it contributes no section and consumes no budget.

An included file renders as "--- \(name) ---
\(text)" and sections are joined with "

".

The block header is exactly "Project guidelines from \(directory). They supplement the rules above; where they conflict, the Droppy Code rules take priority." followed by a newline then the joined sections.
Returns nil when no sections were produced, i.e. neither file present or both empty.
systemPromptBlock() re-renders only when the [name: FileState] map differs from the stored one, so an unchanged project pays two stat calls and nothing else per request.

resolvedFile refuses a name whose symlink target resolves outside the working directory: candidate.path must equal resolvedRoot or start with resolvedRoot + "/"; it also refuses directories and non-regular files.
The repository is never scanned; only these two names at the root are looked up, never a parent directory.
boundedData reads at most perFileLimit + 1 bytes (16001) so oversize is detected without reading the whole file; a read throw returns nil, which becomes the 'Could not load' section.
unresolved_questions: The caller is not in this bundle: which native API session type invokes systemPromptBlock(), and where the block sits relative to the rest of the system prompt, is not visible here. The header wording 'They supplement the rules above' implies it is appended after the base rules.
The 'read_file tool' named in the two fallback strings is assumed to be the tool the native API sessions expose; its definition is in another file.

Antigravity rows: "Gemini 3.8 Flash", "Gemini 3.7 Flash", "Gemini 3.6 Flash", "Gemini 3.1 Pro", "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)", "Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)", "GPT-OSS 120B"
Copilot row: id "auto", name "Auto", detail "Copilot picks the model for each request", isDefault true
Pi row: id "default", name "Default", detail "The model pi itself is set to"
isChecking on ProviderStatus drives a spinner while refresh(_:) runs; loadingCatalogs, loadingLimits, loadingCredits, isRefreshing, signingIn and redeemingReset drive the Providers page's busy states
feature_notes: claudeEfforts = ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"], applied to default, opus, claude-fable-5-1[1m] and sonnet, but NOT to haiku, which has no efforts and no fastTier.
Claude seed ids verbatim: "default" (fastTier "fast", isDefault true), "opus" (fastTier "fast"), "claude-fable-5-1[1m]" (no fastTier), "sonnet", "haiku".

isStaleClaudeSeed treats a cached Claude list as the stale earlier seed when it is empty or every id is in {"default", "opus", "sonnet", "haiku"}; such a list is replaced with claudeSeed at init so old installs gain the Fable row, while a live list without Fable is left alone.
mergedClaudeCatalog never drops a seed row: a live row with the same id lends non-empty efforts, non-empty detail, non-nil fastTier and non-nil defaultEffort; a live row the seed lacks is appended.

mergedACPCatalog (cursor, opencode, grok, devin): rows the live list dropped go away, but a live row with EMPTY efforts inherits efforts, and inherits defaultEffort and fastTier only when its own is nil, from the cached row with the same id; if the cached list is empty the live list is used as is. Rationale in the file: an ACP session reports the effort scale of the model it runs on, not of every model it lists (Cursor and OpenCode send only the current model's thought_level).

deepseekSeed ids: "deepseek-v4-pro", "deepseek-flash". metaSeed ids: "muse-spark-1.3", "muse-spark-1.3-contributor", "muse-spark-1.2", "muse-spark-1.2-contributor", "muse-spark-1.1". zaiSeed ids: "glm-5.3", "glm-5.3-flash". All three are built through each API's option(for:) table so seeds cannot disagree with live lists.

Antigravity efforts per row: gemini-3.8-flash / gemini-3.7-flash / gemini-3.6-flash each ["low", "medium", "high"] with defaultEffort "high"; gemini-3.1-pro ["low", "high"] defaultEffort "high"; claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-6-thinking have empty efforts; gpt-oss-120b ["medium"] defaultEffort "medium". gemini-3.8-flash is isDefault. Source noted as `agy models`.
An Antigravity catalog cached with per-effort duplicate ids, i.e. any id ending in "-high", "-medium" or "-low", is discarded at init and replaced with antigravitySeed.
Pi seed efforts: ["off", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"], defaultEffort "medium", isDefault true.

catalogFreshness = 6 * 3600 seconds (6 hours). commandFreshness = 600 seconds (10 minutes). Plan-limit and credit reads are throttled to once per 60 seconds unless forced. The plan-limit watchdog clears the loading flag after 25 seconds.
probeWidth = 4: refreshAll runs a sliding window of 4 concurrent provider probes, starting the next provider as each one finishes.
refresh runs the version probe and the auth probe one after the other, not concurrently, to halve the simultaneous process count.

countsAsInstalled returns TRUE when no status exists yet, so the launch screen's first chat finds providers before bootstrap() has probed them; a strict read there previously found no pair and no provider.

When CaptureRun.isEnabled, status(_:) returns a synthetic ProviderStatus(executable: file URL /usr/bin/true, auth: .signedIn(nil), apiKeyConfigured: true), no catalogs or dates are read or written, and loadCommands returns immediately.
At init, cached catalogs are re-ordered through ACPSession.orderedEfforts so a list cached high-to-low (Grok's was) reads low-to-high for the effort slider.

executable(for:) returns nil for API-key providers; when a custom binary path from settings is set it is resolved through which() and, if that fails, NO fallback list is consulted, because fallbacks apply only when the custom path is empty. It also returns nil when both the custom path and provider.executableName are empty.
Copilot fallback path: <GH_DATA_DIR, else XDG_DATA_HOME/gh, else ~/.local/share/gh>/copilot/copilot.

Command Code fallbacks, in order: which("command-code"), which("commandcode"), which("cmd"), then the cross product of {~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, ~/.volta/bin} with {"command-code", "cmd"}.
Pi fallbacks in order: ~/.npm-global/bin/pi, /opt/homebrew/bin/pi, /usr/local/bin/pi, ~/.local/bin/pi, ~/.volta/bin/pi, ~/.bun/bin/pi. Other providers have no fallbacks.

environment(for:) prepends the executable's own directory to PATH only when it is not already a PATH element; sets COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY from settings for commandcode (documented as taking precedence over the `cmd login` in ~/.commandcode/auth.json); merges MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment() for opencode so connected MCP servers arrive as config content rather than a config file edit; sets GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH from MCPProviderConfig.geminiSettingsPath() for antigravity.

signIn: refuses when another sign-in is in flight or the provider is API-key based; runs provider.loginCommand split on whitespace with the first word dropped as the argument list, with a 300-second timeout; on success re-runs refresh, refreshPlanLimits(force: true) and loadCatalog(force: true); on failure returns the last non-empty line of stripANSI(output + errorOutput).

refreshEverything: guarded by isRefreshing; runs refreshAll, then forced plan-limit reads for every provider whose auth is not .signedOut, then a concurrent forced catalog load for every installed provider, ACP providers included, because they only list models from a session of their own.

refreshAPIProvider: an empty key gives ProviderStatus(auth: .signedOut) with no apiKeyConfigured; deepseek, meta and zai validate the key and set version "API" with apiKeyConfigured true; a valid DeepSeek key triggers a forced credits read, an invalid one clears credits[.deepseek] and creditsFetchedAt[.deepseek]; a valid Z.ai key triggers a forced plan-limits read, an invalid one clears planLimits[.zai] and limitsFetchedAt[.zai]; any other API provider is set .signedIn(nil) with apiKeyConfigured true without validating.
model(_:for:) falls back to the id text before the first '[' so a legacy parameterized Cursor id such as model[effort=...] still resolves to the base row.
defaultModel prefers settings.lastModel(for:) when it resolves, else the row with isDefault, else the first row.

loadCatalog re-probes when forced; when the list is still a recognized seed (claude and codex always; copilot when it equals exactly [copilotAuto]; commandcode when it equals commandcodeSeed; pi when it equals piSeed; opencode when lacksEffortWalk); when the cached list is older than catalogFreshness, where a list with no stored date counts as stale only if the list is non-empty; or when the list is empty.
lacksEffortWalk: a list with at most one row carrying non-empty efforts is treated as pre-effort-walk and re-probed.

Per-provider live catalog sources: claude through ClaudeSession.handshake run in FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory (models are the same from any folder); codex CodexSession.listModels; antigravity AntigravitySession.listModels; copilot CopilotSession.listModels; commandcode CommandCodeAPI.listModels; pi PiCLI.listModels; cursor, opencode, grok and devin ACPSession.probeModels; deepseek, meta and zai return nil here and are handled by loadAPICatalog.

attemptedCatalogs is marked only after a non-empty list arrives, so a probe that came back empty (a cold CLI losing to its handshake timeout) is retried on the next ask; loadAPICatalog by contrast inserts into attemptedCatalogs before the fetch, once a key exists.
loadAPICatalog seeds the catalog first when empty so API providers stay usable offline, then fetches; an empty API key stops after the seed.

consumeResetCredit sets redeemingReset to the credit id or, when nil, provider.rawValue; codex redeems through CodexSession.consumeResetCredit then re-reads CodexSession.readPlanLimits into planLimits[.codex]; zai redeems through ZaiAPI.consumeResetCredit, requiring a non-empty key and a non-nil creditID, then re-reads ZaiAPI.planLimits; any other provider throws ResetCreditError.unknownOutcome, and a missing codex executable throws ResetCreditError.codexUnavailable.

refreshPlanLimits: gated by PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits; a forced read arriving while a read is out is remembered in forcedLimitReads and replayed by drainedForcedRead when the outstanding read finishes, rather than dropped.
refreshCredits uses CommandCodeAPI.apiKey(environment:) for Command Code, that is the CLI's own login, rather than the Settings key; an empty key clears credits[provider].
invalidateCredits and invalidatePlanLimits only clear the fetch timestamps so the next look re-reads; invalidatePlanLimits applies only to API-key providers that expose limits.
updateCatalog writes nothing when the merged list is empty or identical to the cached list; otherwise it re-encodes the WHOLE catalogs dictionary into "providerModelCatalogs".
commandKey(provider, directory) = provider.rawValue + "\n" + directory, so commands are cached per provider and per working directory.

loadCommands runs only for codex and claude, is skipped entirely under a capture run, de-duplicates concurrent loads by awaiting the in-flight Task for the same key, and records error.localizedDescription into commandErrors on failure. Codex uses CodexSession.listCommands, Claude uses ClaudeSession.handshake(...).commands.
version(): runs `--version` with a 20-second timeout and extracts the first match of the regex \\d+\\.\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?(?:[-.][0-9A-Za-z]+)? from stripANSI(output + errorOutput).

auth() per provider: codex requires succeeded AND a case-insensitive "logged in"; claude parses stdout as JSON, needs "loggedIn" == true and takes the account from "email"; cursor matches the regex "Logged in as (\\S+)", reads "not logged in" as signed out and anything else as unknown; devin reads "not logged in" as out, requires "logged in" else unknown, and takes the account from the "Name:" line; opencode parses `auth list`, keeping the lines before the first line containing "Environment", taking lines whose trimmed text starts with U+25CF (black circle), and stripping a trailing " api" or " oauth" (case-insensitive) from the first credential name; grok reads ~/.grok/auth.json and prefers a non-empty "email", then a non-empty "first_name", else .signedIn(nil), with an empty root object meaning signed out and an unreadable file meaning unknown; antigravity, copilot, commandcode and pi delegate to their own authStatus; deepseek, meta and zai return .unknown.
devinAccount scans lines for one whose lowercased trim starts with "name:" and returns the remainder trimmed, or nil when empty.
updateCommands evicts the least-recently-fetched key, clearing its commands, fetch date and error, once 32 keys are held and a genuinely new key arrives.
recordCommand moves an existing name to the front, keeps only the first 100 per provider, and writes the whole map back to defaults immediately.

ModelOption's exact stored properties and Codable coding keys are not visible here, so the on-disk JSON shape under "providerModelCatalogs" cannot be spelled out.
PlanLimits, PlanLimits.ResetOutcome, ProviderCredits, ResetCreditError and the ProviderSettings protocol are declared elsewhere; only the members used here are established.
A comment claims a live Claude list always names `opus[1m]`, but no code in this file references that id, so the claim could not be verified here.

refreshPlanLimits repeats its `PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits(provider), !loadingLimits.contains(provider)` guard after the API-key branch; the second check is redundant given the first guard, so it is dead but harmless.

purpose: Declares the contract every provider adapter implements: the per-turn input, the launch configuration, the normalized ProviderEvent stream a thread consumes, the ProviderSession protocol itself, ProviderError's user-facing messages, and the ToolTitles helpers for shell unwrapping, relative paths and diff stats.
key_symbols: struct TurnInput: Sendable (text, images, model, effort, serviceTier, fastMode, runtimeMode, interactionMode, isFinalReport, command)

struct SessionConfiguration: Sendable (provider, executable, workingDirectory, environment, resumeID, resumeAt, model, effort, fastMode, runtimeMode, interactionMode, apiKey, hydra, transcript, isHydraHead, antiSlopEnabled)
struct TranscriptMessage: Sendable with enum Role { case user, case assistant }, var role, var text
struct AgentSpawn: Sendable (id, taskID, toolUseID, description, prompt, model, profile, isBackground)
enum ProviderEvent: Sendable, with indirect case agentEvent
struct ToolUpdate: Sendable (title, detail, output, status, exitCode, edits, kind)
extension ProviderSession default stopAgent(_:) returning false
enum ToolTitles with unwrapShell(_:), relativePath(_:to:), diffStats(_:)
calls_into: ProviderKind (SessionConfiguration.provider and ProviderError.notInstalled; uses displayName, isAPIKeyBased, loginCommand)
FileEdit, TodoStep, ApprovalRequest, QuestionRequest, ContextUsage, Notice, TurnStatus, ModelOption
state_owned: No runtime state of its own; it defines the value types and the two protocol requirements conforming sessions own: onEvent: ((ProviderEvent) -> Void)? and isRunning: Bool
side_effects: None directly: type declarations plus three pure string and diff helpers
platform_assumptions: ToolTitles.unwrapShell hard-codes Unix shell wrappers and absolute paths, in this order: "/bin/zsh -lc ", "/bin/bash -lc ", "bash -lc ", "zsh -lc ", "/bin/sh -c ", "sh -c " - zsh first because providers wrap commands in the macOS default login shell
The single-quote un-escape handles the POSIX shell idiom '\'' specifically
relativePath assumes '/' path separators
@MainActor protocol isolation, Sendable conformance and an indirect enum case are Swift concurrency and language features
ui_elements: ProviderError.errorDescription strings: for an API-key provider "\(provider.displayName) needs an API key. Add one in Settings \u2192 Providers \u2192 \(provider.displayName)."; for a CLI provider "\(provider.displayName) is not installed. Install it and sign in with `\(provider.loginCommand)`." with backticks around the command; "The agent session is not running." for .notRunning; the raw message for .failed
feature_notes: TurnInput defaults: serviceTier = nil, fastMode = false, isFinalReport = false. serviceTier is documented as a Codex service tier that is the fast tier, the literal "default", or nil when the model has none. fastMode maps to Cursor ACP's Fast variant (model_config / fast) and other providers ignore it.
isFinalReport marks a Hydra head past its budget answering for the last time: one reply with no tools, where the session can arrange that.

SessionConfiguration defaults: fastMode = false, transcript = [], isHydraHead = false, antiSlopEnabled = true. apiKey is how the native API providers (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai) authenticate instead of a CLI. transcript replays the conversation into a provider that keeps nothing between launches, since the API providers hold history in memory only.
resumeID plus resumeAt let a session resume an earlier provider session, optionally at a point.

hydra: HydraLaunch? is set while Hydra is on for the thread; providers that run heads of their own define them at launch on the pair's model and effort and steer the lead towards them. isHydraHead marks a thread that Droppy Code itself runs as a head, so the session paces it and tells a head that keeps reading without changing anything to act.

AgentSpawn.isBackground defaults to true; a foreground head is finished by its tool result, a background one only by the provider saying so. taskID is Claude's task id, which is what stops the head, and is nil where `id` does that job. `profile` carries the head profile a spawn was routed to: Claude's and Copilot's agent definitions are one per profile, and Codex's spawn call carries the profile's model and effort, which the session matches back.

ProviderEvent cases verbatim: sessionReady(sessionID: String), turnStarted(providerTurnID: String?), messageDelta(id:text:), messageCompleted(id:text:), reasoningDelta(id:text:), reasoningCompleted(id:text:), toolStarted(id:call:), toolOutput(id:text:), toolUpdated(id:update:), planDelta(id:text:), planCompleted(id:markdown:), todos([TodoStep]), approval(ApprovalRequest), question(QuestionRequest), requestResolved(id:), usage(ContextUsage), diff(String), notice(Notice), usageLimit(resetsAt: Date?), modeChanged(InteractionMode), models([ModelOption], current: String?), commands([SlashCommand]), title(String), assistantMessageID(String), turnCompleted(status: TurnStatus, error: String?), exited(error: String?), agentStarted(AgentSpawn), indirect agentEvent(agentID: String, ProviderEvent), agentProgress(agentID:summary:lastTool:tokens:toolCalls:), agentFinished(agentID:status:summary:).
usageLimit carries resetsAt: Date? and means the account's usage limit is spent and the turn stops until it resets, at the time given when known.
agentProgress is the provider's word on a running head: a progress note, its last tool, its token spend and tool-call count, all optional.

ProviderSession protocol requirements: start() async throws -> String returning the session id, send(_ input: TurnInput) async throws, interrupt() async, resolveApproval(_ requestID: String, optionID: String), answerQuestion(_ requestID: String, answers: [String: [String]]), compact() async throws, stop(), and stopAgent(_ id: String) async -> Bool, which has a default implementation returning false so an adapter that cannot stop a head need not implement it.
answerQuestion takes answers as [String: [String]], that is several selected values per question key.
ToolUpdate carries only optionals, so an adapter patches whichever of title, detail, output, status, exitCode, edits or kind it learned.

ToolTitles.unwrapShell trims whitespace and newlines first, strips the first matching prefix, then, when the remainder is at least 2 characters and begins and ends with the same quote character (' or "), drops both quotes; for single quotes it additionally replaces the shell escape sequence '\\'' with a single quote. A command with no known prefix is returned trimmed.
ToolTitles.relativePath normalizes the root by appending '/' when it is missing and strips that prefix; a path outside the root is returned unchanged.

ToolTitles.diffStats splits on "\n" WITHOUT omitting empty subsequences, skips lines starting with "+++" or "---", and counts every remaining line starting with "+" as an addition and every one starting with "-" as a deletion, returning the tuple (additions: Int, deletions: Int). Note it does not skip "@@" hunk headers, which start with neither sign.
unresolved_questions: The payload types ToolCall, FileEdit, TodoStep, ApprovalRequest, QuestionRequest, ContextUsage, Notice, TurnStatus, Attachment, RuntimeMode, InteractionMode, HydraLaunch and SlashCommand are declared in other files, so their fields and exact string values are not established here.
Which adapters actually implement stopAgent rather than taking the default false cannot be told from this file.
Whether antiSlopEnabled gates a prompt block, a post-processing pass or both is not determinable here; only its default of true is visible.
TurnInput.effort and SessionConfiguration.effort are plain String?, so the allowed values come from the catalog rows rather than from a type declared here.

purpose: One-shot, tool-free text generation through the Claude or Codex CLI for two jobs: naming a thread from the first message, and writing a commit message from a diff, including a filter that rejects replies reading as sentences instead of titles.
key_symbols: enum Engine: Sendable { case claude(executable:environment:), case codex(executable:environment:model:) }
static func threadTitle(for message: String, engine: Engine) async -> String?
private static func usable(_ candidate: String) -> String?
private static func run(_ prompt: String, engine: Engine, directory: URL) async -> String?
state_owned: No persistent state; the codex path creates a per-call temporary output file
side_effects: Launches the Claude CLI or Codex CLI as a subprocess with the prompt on stdin
Creates and then removes a temporary file named "droppy-code-<UUID>.txt" in the system temporary directory (codex path only)
platform_assumptions: External CLI binaries located by URL and executed through Shell.run
FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory used as the working directory for title generation
feature_notes: Title prompt rules: "3 to 7 words, under 40 characters, sentence case, no quotes, no trailing punctuation"; the request text is truncated with .prefix(4_000)
Title cleanup: TextCleanup.singleLine(text, limit: 60) then trimming the character set "\"'`*#. "
If the cleaned reply fails the usable() filter, the first non-empty line of the raw reply is trimmed the same way and retried
usable() rejects: empty, longer than 64 characters, more than 9 whitespace-separated words, containing a newline or "?", ending in one of ":;,!…"

usable() rejects openers ["i ", "i'", "sorry", "sure", "here", "please", "could you", "can you", "what ", "it seems", "it looks", "unfortunately", "there is no", "not enough", "need more", "maybe ", "the request", "this request"]
usable() rejects phrases ["more context", "meaningful title", "as an ai", "cannot", "can't", "unable to"]

Commit prompt rules: an imperative subject line of at most 72 characters with no trailing period, optionally a blank line plus a few short bullets, reply with the message only without code fences; summary truncated to 6_000 characters and patch to 40_000
Commit output strips every "```" occurrence and trims whitespace; an empty result becomes nil

Claude engine flags: ["-p", "--output-format", "text", "--model", "haiku", "--tools", "", "--disable-slash-commands", "--strict-mcp-config", "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", "--no-session-persistence"] with timeout 120 and the prompt on stdin, reading result.trimmedOutput

Codex engine flags: ["exec", "--ephemeral", "--skip-git-repo-check", "-s", "read-only", "--model", <model>, "--config", "model_reasoning_effort=\"low\"", "--output-last-message", <temp path>, "-"] with timeout 180; the answer is read back from the output file rather than stdout
Both engines return nil when the process fails (result.succeeded false) or produces empty output
The usable() doc comment cites a real failure: "I need more context to create a meaningful title. What spec…" once reached a chat name
unresolved_questions: Which callers choose the claude versus codex Engine, and how the executable URL and environment are resolved, live outside this bundle

purpose: A small provider-agnostic namespace that recognizes a usage-limit refusal in an error message, extracts the reset time it carries (Unix timestamp after a pipe, or a clock time with optional timezone), and formats a reset Date as friendly user-facing text.
key_symbols: static func matches(_ text: String) -> Bool
static func resetTime(in text: String, now: Date = .now) -> Date?
static func format(_ date: Date) -> String
calls_into: Used by ClaudeSession.handleResult and its rate_limit_event handling in the same bundle
state_owned: None: a stateless enum namespace with only static functions
side_effects: None: pure text and date computation, no I/O
platform_assumptions: Foundation/ICU date formatting with the user's current Calendar and locale (formatted(date: .omitted, time: .shortened) produces the locale's short time)
NSRegularExpression-backed String range matching including the (?i) inline flag
Calendar.current for today/tomorrow checks, so results depend on the device's time zone unless the text named one
persisted_fields: None
ui_elements: format() output shapes: the short time alone for today (for example "3:31 PM"), "tomorrow at <time>", "<Weekday> at <time>" (for example "Thursday at 9:00 AM") within the next 6 days, otherwise abbreviated date plus short time
feature_notes: matches() lowercases the text and returns true on any of: "usage limit", "hit your limit", "usage_limit", "limit reached", "out of extra usage"
Timestamp form: regex \|\s*(\d{9,}) (at least 9 digits after a pipe), as in "usage limit reached|1757865600"; values greater than 1e11 are treated as milliseconds and divided by 1000
Clock form: regex (?i)resets?(?:\s+at)?\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm), matching "resets 3pm" or "resets at 3:30 pm"
12-hour conversion: PM with hour < 12 adds 12; AM with hour == 12 becomes 0; missing minutes default to 0
A timezone in parentheses matching \(([A-Za-z_]+/[A-Za-z_]+)\) (for example "(America/New_York)") overrides Calendar.current.timeZone for the computed reset
The clock time is resolved as the next matching time strictly after `now` using Calendar.nextDate(after:matching:matchingPolicy:.nextTime)
The weekday branch of format() compares against a 6-day horizon computed from Date.now (not from the passed date), so a date more than 6 days out falls through to the abbreviated date form
resetTime returns nil when neither pattern matches, and also when the matched clock digits fail to parse as an hour
unresolved_questions: The `now` parameter defaults to .now but format() always uses Date.now for its 6-day horizon rather than an injectable reference, so the two are not consistently testable; whether tests rely on this is not determinable from this file
Which providers besides Claude feed text into matches() cannot be established from this file alone

writeSynchronously clears the pending entry for that URL then does queue.sync

deleteDocuments(ids) returns early on an empty array, forgets each prefetch entry, and performs one DiskWriter.removeSynchronously([URL]) hop that also clears pending saves for those URLs so a deleted thread cannot be resurrected by a queued save

feature_notes: TokenSpendTracker.spend(total:before:): when unseeded it sets seeded = true and lastTotal = max(0, min(total, before)); every call returns max(0, total - lastTotal) and then sets lastTotal = max(0, total) via defer, so a counter drop from compaction or a reused session object reseeds silently and records nothing

TokenSpendTracker.seedBaseline(total:) is a no-op once seeded; otherwise it sets seeded = true and lastTotal = max(0, total) and counts nothing, for a resumed session whose first reported total is inherited history rather than spend
record(codexSpend:rolloutID:on:) returns without recording when rolloutID.isEmpty, and lowercases the id before storing it

The private record(spend:codexRollout:on:) ignores spend <= 0, adds to both state.daily[day] and dailyTotals[day], adds to state.liveCodex[identity] only for Codex, and schedules at most one debounced save

The live save debounce is exactly Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2)); the task clears liveSave then calls LiveSpendStateStore.save(state). flushLiveSpend cancels the pending task, nils it and saves immediately, for app quit
refreshIfNeeded runs the Codex history scan exactly once per process behind didStartLoad; after that only live recording refreshes the grid

mergedTotals starts from state.legacyDaily, then adds state.daily, then historyDaily, day by day

Scan window: a rollout file is considered only when its mtime >= (now minus historyMonths = 12 months) and mtime < launchDate; files written after launch are skipped because live recording already owns them
tailBytes = 131_072 (128 KB) is read from the end of each rollout; headBytes = 8 * 1_048_576 (8 MB) is the budget for inheritedTotal, read in 512 * 1024 byte chunks

A file's contribution is its final token_count total_tokens minus inheritedTotal(at:), floored at 0 with max(0, own), attributed to the day of that event's timestamp; a tail whose token_count line has no parsable day yields no contribution at all

inheritedTotal scans the head for the FIRST token_count line and returns max(0, total_tokens - last_token_usage.total_tokens), which is what a resumed thread carried in before its own request; last defaults to 0 when last_token_usage is absent

Only lines containing the literal "token_count" are JSON-decoded, in both the head (byte-slice search for the marker Data) and the tail (String.contains, iterating split lines reversed so the newest event wins)
The tail is decoded with String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self), lossy on purpose so one stray byte cannot throw away an intact token_count line

A cached fingerprint is reused only when both mtime == known.mtime (as timeIntervalSince1970) and size == known.size; an empty cached identity is recomputed from the path at reuse time but not written back
After the walk, fingerprints are filtered down to paths actually seen, so deleted rollouts stop contributing

reconcile(): per rollout identity, files are sorted by day descending and the settled live amount is cleared against the newest day's growth first with cleared = min(remaining, file.tokens); a live amount larger than the scanned growth leaves the rest unclaimed rather than going negative; it is recomputed from the fingerprints on every scan so repeated scans and restarts land the same numbers

LiveSpendStateStore.load folds the previous process's liveCodex into settledCodex and then clears liveCodex, so this process's own in-flight rollouts are never subtracted twice; when the file is missing it falls back to reading the v1 defaults key into legacyDaily

CodexFileFingerprint.rolloutIdentity finds the LAST UUID-shaped substring in the file name with the pattern "[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}" using options [.regularExpression, .backwards], lowercased; with no match it falls back to the full path, which then reconciles only with itself
eventDate tries an ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] and then one with [.withInternetDateTime], built per call because ISO8601DateFormatter is not Sendable

Grid build: rangeStart is January 1 of now's year, rangeEnd is rangeStart plus one year minus one day, tomorrow is startOfToday plus one day; leadingGap = (weekday(rangeStart) - firstWeekday + 7) % 7 and gridStart = rangeStart minus leadingGap days; cells outside [rangeStart, rangeEnd] are nil
Grid totals are collected only for days from rangeStart through startOfToday, so future days always read 0

Daily mode colors each cell by its own day total; weekly mode sums the column and writes that sum into all seven rows (nil cells get 0); cumulative mode carries a running total forward and writes it into every cell including nil ones
